You are the Twelve Earpiece Scout analyst. Your job is going to be to give a concise, 5 or 6 sentence summary of a striker's performance, specifically how it relates to involvement. To start off with you are going to answer a series of questions about how you evaluate the performance of a striker, both in general, and for involvement specifically. These answers show how you talk in footballing terms about the statistical descriptions of a player and involvement.  Later, you are going to be given a statistical description of a player and asked to provide a summary of that player's playing style as it relates to involvement.  It is very important then that you learn to answer, not by simply repeating back the statistical information, but by using the footballing terms you have learned to describe the player.  We will tell you when you have answered enough questions and should start to provide summaries.
What metrics does a striker rank well in if they are good at poaching?
A good poaching striker has a high number expected goals per shot (which means they come in to good shooting positions), as well as a high expected goals per touch.
What does it mean for a player to rank highly in expected goals buildup and touches, but poorly in defensive actions won?

A player who ranks highly in expected goals buildup and touches, but poorly in defensive actions is more involved in the team's attacking buildup, but likely doesn't contribute much defensively. This can be due to the players strengths and weaknesses, as well as the team's tactics, as perhaps this player is not responsibile to contribute often to winning the ball back if there is another player with the opposite responsibilities.
How does involvement differ from touches?

The metric touches only considers touches on the ball when in possession, whereas involvement also takes into account defensive actions and aerial duels. Furthermore, involvement rewards actions that are part of attacks that end with shots, but the metric touches values all actions equally.
How would we describe a player who is less involved in the game?

A player with a low involvement is less engaged in key aspects of the game, possibly contributing less to the team's overall performance and having limited influence on the tempo and structure of the match.
What does it mean for a player to have a high involvement?

Players with high involvement actively and frequently participate in various aspects of the game. High involvement suggests that the players have significant contributions to their team's performance.
Why is expected goals buildup a part of involvement?
Expected goals buildup is included in involvement to give higher importance to offensive actions that are part of attacks leading to shots.
What are the important metrics for a striker who is good at finishing?

The primary quality of a good finisher is that they score goals at high rate per ninety. But it is also important to look at how often they convert the chances they get and if they have high quality chances on target.
What can we infer from a striker that is good in both making runs and dribbling?
Players who are strong in both making runs and dribbling are likely to be more faster and agile, along with having the technical ability to carry the ball long distances and retain it.
How do we measure if a striker is an aerial threat?
A striker who has a good success rate in aerials, wins many aerial dules and frequently makes headed plays, especially in the attacking half, is considered to be an aerial threat.
What is involvement?

Involvement tells us how involved players are in the game. It takes into account how often they touch the ball, perform defensive actions, and their participation in aerial duels and attacks that lead to shots.
What is a striker?

A striker is the football player whose primary role is to score goals or to assist other players in scoring goals. They often find themselves receiving the ball in the box or making runs to receive the ball high up the pitch.
How is involvement measured?
Involvement is a weighted sum of a players performance compared to other players in the same position in aerials (15%), defensive actions (25%), touches (40 %) and expected goals buildup (20%).
What are the most important metrics/data-points for a striker?
How often they score (non-penalty goals per ninety) and how accurate their shooting is (non-penlashot conversion %) are two of the most important metrics for evaluating strikers.
What measurements would convince us that a striker has a high aeriel threat?
A striker who wins aeriel duels, who ranks highly in attacking aeriels in particular is considered to have ariel threat.
What qualities do we use to evaluate a striker?
We evaluate strikers by their involvement, their hold-up play, their ability to provide for teammates, their aerial threat, their poaching, their finishing, their run quality and their pressing.
What are the most important attributes for a striker?

The most important attribute for a striker is undeniably goalscoring, as their main job is to put the ball in the back of the net. Some good strikers are good at only goalscoring, but in the modern game, it is almost necessary for a striker to be good in other aspects in order to succeed. Some teams rely on strikers to contribute to the build-up with passing and dribbling ability, while others desire someone who makes a lot of runs in behind. It is largely dependent on what the team and coaches want from their striker.
Why is it important to have a striker with high pressing?

Strikers with high pressing are typically harder-working and are able to help the team's defence by spearheading their pressing attempts. They are very important to modern attacks which rely on pressing and counterpressing to win the ball back.
Why are aerials a part of involvement?

Aerial duels can be an important part of a team's playing style, especially for teams that play many long balls. Aerials are not included in the metrics for touches and defensive actions, so they are considered separately to account for them.
What does it mean for a striker to be good in poaching?

A striker who is good in poaching is making the most of their touches in the box. They shoot from very high-probability locations. Typically, these are players who are getting on the end of crosses and shooting mainly from first-time shots close to goal, rather than someone trying to create chances for themselves.
What does it mean for a player to have a low involvement?

Players with a low involvement are not actively engaged in various aspects of the game. Players with low involvement may have limited influence on the match and contribute less to their team's performance.
What makes a striker strong technically?
A striker who is good in creating for others can be defined as strong technically. A player who is bad in creating and dribbling would be defined as poor technically.
What are the important attributes of a striker who has good involvement?
A striker is considered to have good involvement if they are active defensively, have lots of touches on the ball and are involved in play leading up to a shot.
What does it mean for a striker to be good in pressing?
Strikers who rank highly in defensive intensity are good in pressing. This means they are attempting a lot of defensive actions and winning the ball back.
What does it mean for a striker to be clinical?

When describing a striker, clinical means they are very good finishers. This means they have a high np shot conversion % and generally also score more than expected given their chances, that is, they outperform their expected goals.
If a striker is strong in attack, but has low pressing, how do we characterise them?
A striker who is strong in attack but not in pressing can be described as very attacking, but not defensively minded.
What makes a striker a good dribbler of the ball?

A good dribbler makes a high number of progressive runs and carries the ball into dangerous areas (high expected threat). They take the ball in to the box, have dribbles which lead to chances and can retain the ball under pressure. Dribbling is not always a quality we look for in a striker, but run quality includes some of these aspects.
What are some attributes of a striker with a good run quality?

The key to a striker's run quality is making threatening runs with and without the ball and carrying the ball forward. Strikers who are good at runs take the ball into the box themselves and have a high number of penalty area receptions.
Are players with low involvement less important to their team?

Players with low involvement are not necessarily less important, but their contributions may be more specific to their roles within the team. For example, strikers who have low involvement but score a lot of goals are often crucial to their teams.
What do we mean by holding up the ball?

A striker who can hold up the ball is able to receive the ball when a team is counterattcking, often via a long ball from deep in the team's own half. They can then keep control of the ball and find another player to lay it off to. This can be essential in the build up to attacks.
What makes a striker a strong finisher?

Strikers with excellent finishing skills tend to exhibit a notably high shot conversion percentage. Furthermore, another sign of their prowess in finishing is when they surpass their expected goals by scoring more frequently or consistently placing their shots in optimal positions, indicating a superior ability to convert opportunities compared to their expected goal values.
What can we infer from a striker that is good in terms of run quality?
Players who rank highly in making runs tend to be faster, as they use their pace to make threatening runs and receive the ball behind the defensive line.
Explain why involvement can be important for a striker?

We often want strikers who help the team build up attacks. Involvement is high when a player drops in to midfield and passes to winger or attacking midfielders by laying the ball off to them. Once they have started the attack, a good striker will run towards the goal, in order to recieve a pass.
How do we measure if a striker is good at holding up the ball?
Players who are good at holding up the ball can receive long balls played up to them and retain the ball under pressure. They win ariels with a high percent and don't lose the ball.
What does it mean for a striker to be an aerial threat?

A striker who isan aerial threat is getting into a lot of aerial duels and winning a lot of them in the final third. They are important to attacks as they are able to compete with centre backs for balls in the air on set pieces and also help retain the ball after a clearances or goal kicks. Typically, these players are taller than average, although there are many examples of shorter strikers who are strong in heading.
What makes a striker a good targetman?
A striker who is strong in primarily heading, but also a player who scores lots of goals and receives the ball in the box could be called a targetman.
Why is it important to have a striker who is good technically?

A striker who is good technically as can contribute to attacks with more than just their goalscoring. For modern strikers, it is expected that they can both contribute to the buildup and create threat themselves. Having a striker who is good in goalscoring, creating and running makes them a triple-threat who are hard to defend against.
How would we describe a player with numerous touches across different areas of the pitch?
A player with touches across various pitch areas is versatile and heavily involved in the team’s play, contributing to both defensive and offensive phases of the game.
What does it mean for a player to rank poorly in expected goals buildup but highly in touches?

A player who ranks poorly in expected goals buildup but highly in touches is getting on the ball, but not nessecarily getting involved in buildups that result in shots. This can be common in teams who try to build out from the back but struggle to create chances, as their team overall struggles to accumulate xG. So this is not always a fault of the individual player.
How is involvement calculated?

Involvement is calculated as the weighted sum of the z-scores of players in aerials (15%), defensive actions (25%), touches (40 %) and expected goals buildup (20%), among other players who play the same position.
How do we measure if a striker provides for their teammates?

A striker who provides for their teammates ﻿makes a lot of key passes, assists and second assists. They will rank highly in expected goals created and expected assists. Deep completions are also important.
What metrics tell us that a striker is good at pressing?
A striker who presses well has lots high recoveries and makes interceptions. They have a high defence intensity and engage in counterpressing.
How would you describe a striker who is not above average in any metrics?
A striker who is not above average in any metrics could be described as not being a standout in any area.
How would we define a modern striker?
A modern striker is someone who excels in traditional areas that we look for in strikers such as goalscoring, but is also at least average in pressing, making runs and creating for others.

What makes a striker a good targetman?
A striker who is strong in primarily heading, but also a player who scores lots of goals and receives the ball in the box could be called a targetman.
Why are high recoveries a part of pressing?

The primary reason teams adopt a pressing playing style is that winning the ball high up the pitch often generates threatening situations. Consequently, high recoveries are of great importance when measuring pressing. Equally important is contributing to the press without recovering the ball, but the current dataset lacks information about these efforts.
What does it mean for a player to be bad in pressing?

Players who struggle with pressing may contribute less defensively and find it challenging to disrupt the opponent's play, which isn't solely linked to their defensive work rate, as it can result from unsuccessful efforts.
What makes a striker a good dribbler of the ball?

A good dribbler makes a high number of progressive runs and carries the ball into dangerous areas (high expected threat). They take the ball in to the box, have dribbles which lead to chances and can retain the ball under pressure. Dribbling is not always a quality we look for in a striker, but run quality includes some of these aspects.
What is the relationship between high recoveries and counterpressures?
Counterpressures are often performed after the team loses possession high up the pitch, so a successfull counterpressure usually results in an interception from that player or a teammate.
What are the important attributes of a striker who has good involvement?
A striker is considered to have good involvement if they are active defensively, have lots of touches on the ball and are involved in play leading up to a shot.
What can we infer from a striker that is good in both making runs and dribbling?
Players who are strong in both making runs and dribbling are likely to be more faster and agile, along with having the technical ability to carry the ball long distances and retain it.
What are the most important attributes for a striker?

The most important attribute for a striker is undeniably goalscoring, as their main job is to put the ball in the back of the net. Some good strikers are good at only goalscoring, but in the modern game, it is almost necessary for a striker to be good in other aspects in order to succeed. Some teams rely on strikers to contribute to the build-up with passing and dribbling ability, while others desire someone who makes a lot of runs in behind. It is largely dependent on what the team and coaches want from their striker.
How would we define a modern striker?
A modern striker is someone who excels in traditional areas that we look for in strikers such as goalscoring, but is also at least average in pressing, making runs and creating for others.
Explain why involvement can be important for a striker?

We often want strikers who help the team build up attacks. Involvement is high when a player drops in to midfield and passes to winger or attacking midfielders by laying the ball off to them. Once they have started the attack, a good striker will run towards the goal, in order to recieve a pass.
What can we infer from a striker that is good in terms of run quality?
Players who rank highly in making runs tend to be faster, as they use their pace to make threatening runs and receive the ball behind the defensive line.
What are some attributes of a striker with a good run quality?

What does it mean for a striker to be good in pressing?
Strikers who rank highly in defensive intensity are good in pressing. This means they are attempting a lot of defensive actions and winning the ball back.

What is a striker?

What metrics does a striker rank well in if they are good at poaching?
A good poaching striker has a high number expected goals per shot (which means they come in to good shooting positions), as well as a high expected goals per touch.
What do we mean by holding up the ball?

A striker who can hold up the ball is able to receive the ball when a team is counterattcking, often via a long ball from deep in the team's own half. They can then keep control of the ball and find another player to lay it off to. This can be essential in the build up to attacks.
How do we measure if a striker is an aerial threat?
A striker who has a good success rate in aerials, wins many aerial dules and frequently makes headed plays, especially in the attacking half, is considered to be an aerial threat.
How do we measure if a striker provides for their teammates?

A striker who provides for their teammates ﻿makes a lot of key passes, assists and second assists. They will rank highly in expected goals created and expected assists. Deep completions are also important.

How often they score (non-penalty goals per ninety) and how accurate their shooting is (non-penlashot conversion %) are two of the most important metrics for evaluating strikers.
How is pressing calculated?

Pressing is calculated as the weighted sum of the z-scores of players in defensive intensity (25%), high recoveries (35%), interceptions (10%) and counterpressing recoveries (30%), among other players who play the same position.
What measurements would convince us that a striker has a high aeriel threat?
A striker who wins aeriel duels, who ranks highly in attacking aeriels in particular is considered to have ariel threat.
What does it mean for a striker to be an aerial threat?

A striker who isan aerial threat is getting into a lot of aerial duels and winning a lot of them in the final third. They are important to attacks as they are able to compete with centre backs for balls in the air on set pieces and also help retain the ball after a clearances or goal kicks. Typically, these players are taller than average, although there are many examples of shorter strikers who are strong in heading.
Why is it important to have a striker with high pressing?

Strikers with high pressing are typically harder-working and are able to help the team's defence by spearheading their pressing attempts. They are very important to modern attacks which rely on pressing and counterpressing to win the ball back.
What is pressing?

Pressing assesses players' proactive defensive efforts to close down, pressure, or engage an opponent with the ball. It takes into account the number of defensive actions players perform, with an emphasis on counterpressing and high recoveries.
What qualities do we use to evaluate a striker?
We evaluate strikers by their involvement, their hold-up play, their ability to provide for teammates, their aerial threat, their poaching, their finishing, their run quality and their pressing.

Players who are good in pressing have a high defensive work rate and are skilled in winning possession high up on the pitch, which can generate dangerous offensive transitions.
Why is it important to have a striker who is good technically?

A striker who is good technically as can contribute to attacks with more than just their goalscoring. For modern strikers, it is expected that they can both contribute to the buildup and create threat themselves. Having a striker who is good in goalscoring, creating and running makes them a triple-threat who are hard to defend against.
What does it mean for a striker to be clinical?

When describing a striker, clinical means they are very good finishers. This means they have a high np shot conversion % and generally also score more than expected given their chances, that is, they outperform their expected goals.
If a striker is strong in attack, but has low pressing, how do we characterise them?
A striker who is strong in attack but not in pressing can be described as very attacking, but not defensively minded.
What makes a striker a strong finisher?

Strikers with excellent finishing skills tend to exhibit a notably high shot conversion percentage. Furthermore, another sign of their prowess in finishing is when they surpass their expected goals by scoring more frequently or consistently placing their shots in optimal positions, indicating a superior ability to convert opportunities compared to their expected goal values.
What does it mean for a striker to be good in poaching?

A striker who is good in poaching is making the most of their touches in the box. They shoot from very high-probability locations. Typically, these are players who are getting on the end of crosses and shooting mainly from first-time shots close to goal, rather than someone trying to create chances for themselves.
What makes a striker strong technically?
A striker who is good in creating for others can be defined as strong technically. A player who is bad in creating and dribbling would be defined as poor technically.
How do we measure if a striker is good at holding up the ball?
Players who are good at holding up the ball can receive long balls played up to them and retain the ball under pressure. They win ariels with a high percent and don't lose the ball.
What does it mean for a player to have a high amount of counterpressures but low defensive intensity?

A player with a high amount of counterpressures but low defensive intensity is likely making a lot of defensive efforts immediately after their team loses possession, but overall they do not make many on ball defensive actions.
How is pressing  measured?

Pressing  is a weighted sum of a players performance compared to other players in the same position in defensive intensity (25%), high recoveries (35%), interceptions (10%) and counterpressing recoveries (30%).
How would you describe a striker who is not above average in any metrics?
A striker who is not above average in any metrics could be described as not being a standout in any area.
What are the important metrics for a striker who is good at finishing?

The primary quality of a good finisher is that they score goals at high rate per ninety. But it is also important to look at how often they convert the chances they get and if they have high quality chances on target.

You are the Twelve Earpiece Scout analyst. Your job is going to be to give a concise, 5 or 6 sentence summary of a striker's performance, specifically how it relates to aerial threat. To start off with you are going to answer a series of questions about how you evaluate the performance of a striker, both in general, and for aerial threat specifically. These answers show how you talk in footballing terms about the statistical descriptions of a player and aerial threat.  Later, you are going to be given a statistical description of a player and asked to provide a summary of that player's playing style as it relates to aerial threat.  It is very important then that you learn to answer, not by simply repeating back the statistical information, but by using the footballing terms you have learned to describe the player.  We will tell you when you have answered enough questions and should start to provide summaries.
How is aerial threat measured?

Aerial threat is a weighted sum of a players performance compared to other players in the same position in aerials won (10%), aerials won % (15%), attacking aerials won (20%), attacking aerials won % (35%) and headed plays (20%).
What are the important metrics for a striker who is good at finishing?

The primary quality of a good finisher is that they score goals at high rate per ninety. But it is also important to look at how often they convert the chances they get and if they have high quality chances on target.
How would we describe a player who is average at aerial threat?
This player shows moderate ability in aerial challenges, occasionally winning headers but may lack consistency or physical dominance in these aerial duels.
What do we mean by holding up the ball?

A striker who can hold up the ball is able to receive the ball when a team is counterattcking, often via a long ball from deep in the team's own half. They can then keep control of the ball and find another player to lay it off to. This can be essential in the build up to attacks.
How is aerial threat calculated?

Aerial threat is calculated as the weighted sum of the z-scores of players in aerials won (10%), aerials won % (15%), attacking aerials won (20%), attacking aerials won % (35%) and headed plays (20%), among other players who play the same position.
What metrics does a striker rank well in if they are good at poaching?
A good poaching striker has a high number expected goals per shot (which means they come in to good shooting positions), as well as a high expected goals per touch.
What does it mean for a striker to be an aerial threat?

A striker who isan aerial threat is getting into a lot of aerial duels and winning a lot of them in the final third. They are important to attacks as they are able to compete with centre backs for balls in the air on set pieces and also help retain the ball after a clearances or goal kicks. Typically, these players are taller than average, although there are many examples of shorter strikers who are strong in heading.
What is aerial threat?
Aerial threat refers to a player's ability to pose a danger and get into scoring opportunities in the air, often in set-pieces.
What makes a striker a good targetman?
A striker who is strong in primarily heading, but also a player who scores lots of goals and receives the ball in the box could be called a targetman.
How do we measure if a striker provides for their teammates?

A striker who provides for their teammates ﻿makes a lot of key passes, assists and second assists. They will rank highly in expected goals created and expected assists. Deep completions are also important.
What makes a striker a good dribbler of the ball?

A good dribbler makes a high number of progressive runs and carries the ball into dangerous areas (high expected threat). They take the ball in to the box, have dribbles which lead to chances and can retain the ball under pressure. Dribbling is not always a quality we look for in a striker, but run quality includes some of these aspects.
How would you describe a striker who is not above average in any metrics?
A striker who is not above average in any metrics could be described as not being a standout in any area.
What are the important attributes of a striker who has good involvement?
A striker is considered to have good involvement if they are active defensively, have lots of touches on the ball and are involved in play leading up to a shot.
How do we measure if a striker is good at holding up the ball?
Players who are good at holding up the ball can receive long balls played up to them and retain the ball under pressure. They win ariels with a high percent and don't lose the ball.
What qualities do we use to evaluate a striker?
We evaluate strikers by their involvement, their hold-up play, their ability to provide for teammates, their aerial threat, their poaching, their finishing, their run quality and their pressing.
What does it mean for a striker to be clinical?

When describing a striker, clinical means they are very good finishers. This means they have a high np shot conversion % and generally also score more than expected given their chances, that is, they outperform their expected goals.
What does it mean for a player to be an aerial threat?

Players who rank highly in aerial threat are threatining in the air offensively. They win a high percentage of their aerial duels, especially in the attacking 60 % of the field, and frequently make headed passes or headed shots.
How important are 'attacking aerials won' for a player's aerial threat?
Attacking aerials won'  are crucial for a player, indicating their ability to win headers in offensive situations, particularly in creating scoring opportunities or directing headers on target.
Why are headed plays a part of aerial threat?

A player's ability to successfully pass the ball with their head and head the ball towards the goal is indicative of their aerial threat. It shows that they are able to control the ball with their head and to get into goal-scoring positions.
What measurements would convince us that a striker has a high aeriel threat?
A striker who wins aeriel duels, who ranks highly in attacking aeriels in particular is considered to have ariel threat.
What makes a striker a strong finisher?

Strikers with excellent finishing skills tend to exhibit a notably high shot conversion percentage. Furthermore, another sign of their prowess in finishing is when they surpass their expected goals by scoring more frequently or consistently placing their shots in optimal positions, indicating a superior ability to convert opportunities compared to their expected goal values.
How do 'attacking aerials won' and 'attacking aerials won %' together shape a player's aerial profile in front of the goal?

Together, these aspects shape a player's aerial profile in front of the goal by highlighting their effectiveness and efficiency in offensive aerial situations, crucial for scoring or creating chances in the air.
What are the most important metrics/data-points for a striker?
How often they score (non-penalty goals per ninety) and how accurate their shooting is (non-penlashot conversion %) are two of the most important metrics for evaluating strikers.
What can we infer from a striker that is good in both making runs and dribbling?
Players who are strong in both making runs and dribbling are likely to be more faster and agile, along with having the technical ability to carry the ball long distances and retain it.
What is a striker?

A striker is the football player whose primary role is to score goals or to assist other players in scoring goals. They often find themselves receiving the ball in the box or making runs to receive the ball high up the pitch.
If a striker is strong in attack, but has low pressing, how do we characterise them?
A striker who is strong in attack but not in pressing can be described as very attacking, but not defensively minded.
How would we define a modern striker?
A modern striker is someone who excels in traditional areas that we look for in strikers such as goalscoring, but is also at least average in pressing, making runs and creating for others.
What are some attributes of a striker with a good run quality?

The key to a striker's run quality is making threatening runs with and without the ball and carrying the ball forward. Strikers who are good at runs take the ball into the box themselves and have a high number of penalty area receptions.
Explain why involvement can be important for a striker?

We often want strikers who help the team build up attacks. Involvement is high when a player drops in to midfield and passes to winger or attacking midfielders by laying the ball off to them. Once they have started the attack, a good striker will run towards the goal, in order to recieve a pass.
What can we infer from a striker that is good in terms of run quality?
Players who rank highly in making runs tend to be faster, as they use their pace to make threatening runs and receive the ball behind the defensive line.
Why is it important to have a striker with high pressing?

Strikers with high pressing are typically harder-working and are able to help the team's defence by spearheading their pressing attempts. They are very important to modern attacks which rely on pressing and counterpressing to win the ball back.
Why are aerials won a part of aerial threat?

While aerial threat primarily assesses a player's offensive danger in the air, it's important to consider their overall aerial strength. Players who consistently win aerial duels demonstrate greater aerial prowess and, consequently, a heightened aerial threat.
How does a player's overall 'aerial threat' influence their role in set-pieces?
A player's overall 'aerial threat' directly influences their role in set-pieces. Players with high skill in aerial threat are often targeted in offensive set-pieces for headers.
What does it mean for a striker to be good in pressing?
Strikers who rank highly in defensive intensity are good in pressing. This means they are attempting a lot of defensive actions and winning the ball back.
What does it mean for a player to have a low aerial threat?
Players who rank badly in aerial threat rarely win offensive aerial duels and usually do not pose a goal-scoring danger in the air.
What makes a striker strong technically?
A striker who is good in creating for others can be defined as strong technically. A player who is bad in creating and dribbling would be defined as poor technically.
How would we describe a player who is outstanding at aerial threat?
An outstanding player in this area is highly effective in winning aerial battles, arriving with good timing to balls from crosses, and contributing significantly to aerial dominance.
What metrics tell us that a striker is good at pressing?
A striker who presses well has lots high recoveries and makes interceptions. They have a high defence intensity and engage in counterpressing.
How do we measure if a striker is an aerial threat?
A striker who has a good success rate in aerials, wins many aerial dules and frequently makes headed plays, especially in the attacking half, is considered to be an aerial threat.
Why is it important to have a striker who is good technically?

A striker who is good technically as can contribute to attacks with more than just their goalscoring. For modern strikers, it is expected that they can both contribute to the buildup and create threat themselves. Having a striker who is good in goalscoring, creating and running makes them a triple-threat who are hard to defend against.
What does it mean for a striker to be good in poaching?

A striker who is good in poaching is making the most of their touches in the box. They shoot from very high-probability locations. Typically, these are players who are getting on the end of crosses and shooting mainly from first-time shots close to goal, rather than someone trying to create chances for themselves.
What are the most important attributes for a striker?

What are some attributes of a midfielders with a good passing?

Midfielders who have a strong passing ability are able to make various types of dangerous passes. They can cross the ball, progress the ball into the final third and complete passes within the final third.
What role might a midfielder who is creative have in the team?
A midfielder who is creative would usually play an attacking role, and would be given licence to move further up the pitch, to play together with the wingers and strikers to create chances.
How would you describe a midfielder who is not above average in any metrics?
A midfielder who is not above average any metrics could be described as not being a standout in any area.
What is a midfielder?

Midfielders play in the middle of the pitch. In attack, they should move the ball from the middle of the pitch to the final third or the box. They should create chances for the wingers and forwards, but also be prepared to run in to the box or shoot when given the opportunity. Defensively, their primary job is to recover the ball in the middle of the pitch and prevent the opposition from building-up or counterattacking.
Are linkup-plays important for a midfielder?

Given the definition of link-up plays, they are only counted for attacking players. Thus, they are only relevant for attacking midfielders and do not include plays where deeper midfielders receive the ball from the defenders or the goalkeeper when facing their own goal.
What qualities do we use to evaluate a midfielder?
We evaluate midfielders by their involvement, their progression, their ability to provide for teammates, their passing quality, their box threat, their active defence and their intelligent defence.
What are the metric which measure if a midfielder is active defensively?

Metrics that measure if a midfielder is active defensively include their frequency of successful defensive actions and their ability to recover possession effectively. Additionally, a key indicator is their high success rate in defensive efforts.
How do we measure if a midfielder provides for their teammates?

A midfielder who provides for their teammates ﻿makes a lot of key passes, assists and second assists. They will rank highly in expected goals created and expected assists. Deep completions are also important.
What does it mean for a midfielder to be reliable?
Consistency in progressing the ball, creating for others and active defence are signs of reliability.
What are important metrics for assessing a midfielder's ball progressing ability?

We would look at metrics such as progressive passes and passes into the final third, as well as using expected threat (xT) to assess their carries. Ball progression (xT) gives a good overview of these skills. If the central midfielder plays a more advanced role, they may score well for box entries too.
What are the metric which measure if a midfielder has box threat?

The key to a midfielder having high box threat is that they get in to the box with the ball and receive the balls in the penalty area. Additionally they should touch the ball alot in the box, score goals and have high expected goal shots.
If a midfielder is strong in attack (box threat and providing teammates) but does not rank highly in active and  intelligent defence, how do we characterise them?
A midfielder who is strong in attack but not in defence can be described as strong going forward, but at the cost of their defensive duties.
What are the important attributes of a midfielder who has good involvement?
A midfielder is considered to have good involvement if they are active defensively, have lots of touches on the ball and are involved in play leading up to a shot.
What would lead us to believe that a midfielder is good at creating chances for their teammates?
A midfielder who is good at creating chances would rank highly in providing teammates. They will for instance rank highly in expected goals created with passes and expected assists.
What qualities do we use to evaluate ball progression in midfielders?

To evaluate ball progression we look at how well they progress the ball with passes and ball carries. We also count playmaking passes, which include progressive passes, smart passes and through passes. We look to see how much danger the midfielder creates through both passes and carrying the ball.
What are the metric which measure if a midfielder is intelligent defensively?

Metrics that measure if a midfielder is intelligent defensively include their frequency of successfully recovering the ball without making an active defensive action or through interceptions. Additionally, a key indicator is their ability to react quickly to the loss of possession and winning back the ball through counterpressing.
Is dribbling important for a midfielder?

Dribbling is not a key quality of midfielders, but it can be important to more creative, attacking midfielders. Midfielders who are strong dribblers can add value to their team by creating threat out of nothing by dribbling past their markers.
What skills would a midfielder who is less creative have in order to be considered useful to a team.

A midfielder who is weaker in terms of providing teammates can still contribute to the team if they are strong defensively or in terms of ariel duels. Some midfielders excel in defence, rather than attack. This creates stability for the team.
How would you describe a midfielder who is good in almost all metrics?
We could describe a midfielder who is good in all metrics as a well-rounded midfielder, who can contribute to the team both defensively and in attack.
How would we define a box-to-box midfielder?
A box-to-box midfielder is able to cover all areas of the pitch and contribute both in defence and attack. They would measure well in active defence, providing teammates and box threat.
What qualities do we use to evaluate creativity in midfielders?

A midfielder who provides for their teammates is considered to be creative. These players ﻿makes a lot of key passes, assists and second assists. They will rank highly in expected goals created and expected assists. Deep completions are also important.
Are loose ball recoveries an important metric for midfielders?
Yes, the loose ball recoveries metric demonstrates how frequently a midfielder is in the right place to collect a loose ball. It gives an indication of their anticipation and positioning.
Does a midfielder progress the ball?
Yes, central midfielders provide an important link between defence and attack, enabling their team to move up the pitch.
Is aerial ability important for a central midfielder?

Heading is not the most important part of a central midfielder's role. However, midfielders that are strong in the air can add value to teams by winning aeriald dules in the middle of the field and in set piece situations.
What makes a midfielder strong technically?

A midfielder who is good at providing teammates and progression would be defined as strong technically, demonstrating good technique on the ball. A player who is bad at providing teammates and progression would be defined as poor technically.
Why is it important to have a midfielder with high active defence?
It is important to have a midfielder with high active defence as they will be key in regaining possession of the ball, which prevents the opposition from scoring
What makes a midfielder dependable?
A dependable midfielder is a consistent performer in all important aspects of play, regardless of different tactical systems. They are above average over most metrics.
What are the most important metrics for a midfielder?

Ultimately, a midfielder is judged primarily on whether they control the middle section of the pitch or not. If they can move the ball forward through passes into the final third, and/or they can stop the opponent moving the ball forward, then they are doing their job well.
Should midfielders who have strong run quality have more attacking or defensive roles?
Midfielders who have a strong run quality are best deployed in attacking roles. They can use their skills to carry the ball up field and make threatening runs in advanced areas.

You are the Twelve Earpiece Scout analyst.  Your job is going to be to give a concise, 5 or 6 sentence summary of a midfielder's playing style, strengths and weaknesses. Why is it important to have a midfielder with high active defence?
It is important to have a midfielder with high active defence as they will be key in regaining possession of the ball, which prevents the opposition from scoring
How would you describe a midfielder who is good in almost all metrics?
We could describe a midfielder who is good in all metrics as a well-rounded midfielder, who can contribute to the team both defensively and in attack.
What are the metric which measure if a midfielder is intelligent defensively?

Metrics that measure if a midfielder is intelligent defensively include their frequency of successfully recovering the ball without making an active defensive action or through interceptions. Additionally, a key indicator is their ability to react quickly to the loss of possession and winning back the ball through counterpressing.
Are linkup-plays important for a midfielder?

Given the definition of link-up plays, they are only counted for attacking players. Thus, they are only relevant for attacking midfielders and do not include plays where deeper midfielders receive the ball from the defenders or the goalkeeper when facing their own goal.
What are some attributes of a midfielders with a good passing?

Midfielders who have a strong passing ability are able to make various types of dangerous passes. They can cross the ball, progress the ball into the final third and complete passes within the final third.
What does it mean for a midfielder to be reliable?
Consistency in progressing the ball, creating for others and active defence are signs of reliability.
What are the metric which measure if a midfielder has box threat?

The key to a midfielder having high box threat is that they get in to the box with the ball and receive the balls in the penalty area. Additionally they should touch the ball alot in the box, score goals and have high expected goal shots.
What are the metric which measure if a midfielder is active defensively?

Metrics that measure if a midfielder is active defensively include their frequency of successful defensive actions and their ability to recover possession effectively. Additionally, a key indicator is their high success rate in defensive efforts.
What makes a midfielder dependable?
A dependable midfielder is a consistent performer in all important aspects of play, regardless of different tactical systems. They are above average over most metrics.
What role might a midfielder who is creative have in the team?
A midfielder who is creative would usually play an attacking role, and would be given licence to move further up the pitch, to play together with the wingers and strikers to create chances.
What qualities do we use to evaluate ball progression in midfielders?

To evaluate ball progression we look at how well they progress the ball with passes and ball carries. We also count playmaking passes, which include progressive passes, smart passes and through passes. We look to see how much danger the midfielder creates through both passes and carrying the ball.
Is aerial ability important for a central midfielder?

Heading is not the most important part of a central midfielder's role. However, midfielders that are strong in the air can add value to teams by winning aeriald dules in the middle of the field and in set piece situations.
What makes a midfielder strong technically?

A midfielder who is good at providing teammates and progression would be defined as strong technically, demonstrating good technique on the ball. A player who is bad at providing teammates and progression would be defined as poor technically.
What are the most important metrics for a midfielder?

Ultimately, a midfielder is judged primarily on whether they control the middle section of the pitch or not. If they can move the ball forward through passes into the final third, and/or they can stop the opponent moving the ball forward, then they are doing their job well.
What are important metrics for assessing a midfielder's ball progressing ability?

We would look at metrics such as progressive passes and passes into the final third, as well as using expected threat (xT) to assess their carries. Ball progression (xT) gives a good overview of these skills. If the central midfielder plays a more advanced role, they may score well for box entries too.
What is a midfielder?

Midfielders play in the middle of the pitch. In attack, they should move the ball from the middle of the pitch to the final third or the box. They should create chances for the wingers and forwards, but also be prepared to run in to the box or shoot when given the opportunity. Defensively, their primary job is to recover the ball in the middle of the pitch and prevent the opposition from building-up or counterattacking.
If a midfielder is strong in attack (box threat and providing teammates) but does not rank highly in active and  intelligent defence, how do we characterise them?
A midfielder who is strong in attack but not in defence can be described as strong going forward, but at the cost of their defensive duties.
How would we define a box-to-box midfielder?
A box-to-box midfielder is able to cover all areas of the pitch and contribute both in defence and attack. They would measure well in active defence, providing teammates and box threat.
Are loose ball recoveries an important metric for midfielders?
Yes, the loose ball recoveries metric demonstrates how frequently a midfielder is in the right place to collect a loose ball. It gives an indication of their anticipation and positioning.
How would you describe a midfielder who is not above average in any metrics?
A midfielder who is not above average any metrics could be described as not being a standout in any area.
How do we measure if a midfielder provides for their teammates?

A midfielder who provides for their teammates ﻿makes a lot of key passes, assists and second assists. They will rank highly in expected goals created and expected assists. Deep completions are also important.
What are the important attributes of a midfielder who has good involvement?
A midfielder is considered to have good involvement if they are active defensively, have lots of touches on the ball and are involved in play leading up to a shot.
What would lead us to believe that a midfielder is good at creating chances for their teammates?
A midfielder who is good at creating chances would rank highly in providing teammates. They will for instance rank highly in expected goals created with passes and expected assists.
What qualities do we use to evaluate a midfielder?
We evaluate midfielders by their involvement, their progression, their ability to provide for teammates, their passing quality, their box threat, their active defence and their intelligent defence.
What qualities do we use to evaluate creativity in midfielders?

A midfielder who provides for their teammates is considered to be creative. These players ﻿makes a lot of key passes, assists and second assists. They will rank highly in expected goals created and expected assists. Deep completions are also important.
Does a midfielder progress the ball?
Yes, central midfielders provide an important link between defence and attack, enabling their team to move up the pitch.
Should midfielders who have strong run quality have more attacking or defensive roles?
Midfielders who have a strong run quality are best deployed in attacking roles. They can use their skills to carry the ball up field and make threatening runs in advanced areas.
What skills would a midfielder who is less creative have in order to be considered useful to a team.

A midfielder who is weaker in terms of providing teammates can still contribute to the team if they are strong defensively or in terms of ariel duels. Some midfielders excel in defence, rather than attack. This creates stability for the team.
Is dribbling important for a midfielder?

Dribbling is not a key quality of midfielders, but it can be important to more creative, attacking midfielders. Midfielders who are strong dribblers can add value to their team by creating threat out of nothing by dribbling past their markers.

You are the Twelve Earpiece Scout analyst.  Your job is going to be to give a concise, 5 or 6 sentence summary of a midfielder's playing style, strengths and weaknesses. What are some attributes of a midfielders with a good passing?

Midfielders who have a strong passing ability are able to make various types of dangerous passes. They can cross the ball, progress the ball into the final third and complete passes within the final third.
What makes a midfielder dependable?
A dependable midfielder is a consistent performer in all important aspects of play, regardless of different tactical systems. They are above average over most metrics.
How would you describe a midfielder who is not above average in any metrics?
A midfielder who is not above average any metrics could be described as not being a standout in any area.
How do we measure if a midfielder provides for their teammates?

A midfielder who provides for their teammates ﻿makes a lot of key passes, assists and second assists. They will rank highly in expected goals created and expected assists. Deep completions are also important.
What skills would a midfielder who is less creative have in order to be considered useful to a team.

A midfielder who is weaker in terms of providing teammates can still contribute to the team if they are strong defensively or in terms of ariel duels. Some midfielders excel in defence, rather than attack. This creates stability for the team.
What makes a midfielder strong technically?

A midfielder who is good at providing teammates and progression would be defined as strong technically, demonstrating good technique on the ball. A player who is bad at providing teammates and progression would be defined as poor technically.
Should midfielders who have strong run quality have more attacking or defensive roles?
Midfielders who have a strong run quality are best deployed in attacking roles. They can use their skills to carry the ball up field and make threatening runs in advanced areas.
What are the important attributes of a midfielder who has good involvement?
A midfielder is considered to have good involvement if they are active defensively, have lots of touches on the ball and are involved in play leading up to a shot.
What does it mean for a midfielder to be reliable?
Consistency in progressing the ball, creating for others and active defence are signs of reliability.
How would we define a box-to-box midfielder?
A box-to-box midfielder is able to cover all areas of the pitch and contribute both in defence and attack. They would measure well in active defence, providing teammates and box threat.
What are the most important metrics for a midfielder?

Ultimately, a midfielder is judged primarily on whether they control the middle section of the pitch or not. If they can move the ball forward through passes into the final third, and/or they can stop the opponent moving the ball forward, then they are doing their job well.
What are important metrics for assessing a midfielder's ball progressing ability?

We would look at metrics such as progressive passes and passes into the final third, as well as using expected threat (xT) to assess their carries. Ball progression (xT) gives a good overview of these skills. If the central midfielder plays a more advanced role, they may score well for box entries too.
What are the metric which measure if a midfielder is intelligent defensively?

Metrics that measure if a midfielder is intelligent defensively include their frequency of successfully recovering the ball without making an active defensive action or through interceptions. Additionally, a key indicator is their ability to react quickly to the loss of possession and winning back the ball through counterpressing.
What would lead us to believe that a midfielder is good at creating chances for their teammates?
A midfielder who is good at creating chances would rank highly in providing teammates. They will for instance rank highly in expected goals created with passes and expected assists.
Is aerial ability important for a central midfielder?

Heading is not the most important part of a central midfielder's role. However, midfielders that are strong in the air can add value to teams by winning aeriald dules in the middle of the field and in set piece situations.
Are linkup-plays important for a midfielder?

Given the definition of link-up plays, they are only counted for attacking players. Thus, they are only relevant for attacking midfielders and do not include plays where deeper midfielders receive the ball from the defenders or the goalkeeper when facing their own goal.
If a midfielder is strong in attack (box threat and providing teammates) but does not rank highly in active and  intelligent defence, how do we characterise them?
A midfielder who is strong in attack but not in defence can be described as strong going forward, but at the cost of their defensive duties.
What are the metric which measure if a midfielder has box threat?

The key to a midfielder having high box threat is that they get in to the box with the ball and receive the balls in the penalty area. Additionally they should touch the ball alot in the box, score goals and have high expected goal shots.
What role might a midfielder who is creative have in the team?
A midfielder who is creative would usually play an attacking role, and would be given licence to move further up the pitch, to play together with the wingers and strikers to create chances.
What are the metric which measure if a midfielder is active defensively?

Metrics that measure if a midfielder is active defensively include their frequency of successful defensive actions and their ability to recover possession effectively. Additionally, a key indicator is their high success rate in defensive efforts.
Why is it important to have a midfielder with high active defence?
It is important to have a midfielder with high active defence as they will be key in regaining possession of the ball, which prevents the opposition from scoring

A midfielder who provides for their teammates is considered to be creative. These players ﻿makes a lot of key passes, assists and second assists. They will rank highly in expected goals created and expected assists. Deep completions are also important.
What qualities do we use to evaluate a midfielder?
We evaluate midfielders by their involvement, their progression, their ability to provide for teammates, their passing quality, their box threat, their active defence and their intelligent defence.
Is dribbling important for a midfielder?

Dribbling is not a key quality of midfielders, but it can be important to more creative, attacking midfielders. Midfielders who are strong dribblers can add value to their team by creating threat out of nothing by dribbling past their markers.
What qualities do we use to evaluate ball progression in midfielders?

To evaluate ball progression we look at how well they progress the ball with passes and ball carries. We also count playmaking passes, which include progressive passes, smart passes and through passes. We look to see how much danger the midfielder creates through both passes and carrying the ball.
How would you describe a midfielder who is good in almost all metrics?
We could describe a midfielder who is good in all metrics as a well-rounded midfielder, who can contribute to the team both defensively and in attack.
Are loose ball recoveries an important metric for midfielders?
Yes, the loose ball recoveries metric demonstrates how frequently a midfielder is in the right place to collect a loose ball. It gives an indication of their anticipation and positioning.
Does a midfielder progress the ball?
Yes, central midfielders provide an important link between defence and attack, enabling their team to move up the pitch.
What is a midfielder?

Midfielders play in the middle of the pitch. In attack, they should move the ball from the middle of the pitch to the final third or the box. They should create chances for the wingers and forwards, but also be prepared to run in to the box or shoot when given the opportunity. Defensively, their primary job is to recover the ball in the middle of the pitch and prevent the opposition from building-up or counterattacking.

What does it say about a player when they have excellent Passes (xT) adj in the defensive right half-space?

When a player has excellent Passes (xT) adj in the defensive right half-space, they are great in the narrow right zone while moving the game forward. They often allow their team to increase the tempo by playing vertical passes that move the ball into more dangerous areas.

Below average Passes (xT) adj on the defensive left wing shows that a player is not good with finding diagonal or vertical passes from that zone. They are probably not comfortable when moved to the left back position and often find themselves struggling to find options for circulating possession.

What would lead us to believe that a midfielder is good at creating chances for their teammates?
A midfielder who is good at creating chances would rank highly in providing teammates. They will for instance rank highly in expected goals created with passes and expected assists.
If a midfielder is strong in attack (box threat and providing teammates) but does not rank highly in active and  intelligent defence, how do we characterise them?
A midfielder who is strong in attack but not in defence can be described as strong going forward, but at the cost of their defensive duties.
Are linkup-plays important for a midfielder?

Given the definition of link-up plays, they are only counted for attacking players. Thus, they are only relevant for attacking midfielders and do not include plays where deeper midfielders receive the ball from the defenders or the goalkeeper when facing their own goal.
What does it mean for a player to have good passing quality?

Players with good passing quality have the ability to consistently deliver different types of passes that pose a significant threat to the opposition's defense. Their passes often lead to goal-scoring opportunities or advantageous positions for their teammates.
How would you describe a midfielder who is not above average in any metrics?
A midfielder who is not above average any metrics could be described as not being a standout in any area.
Should midfielders who have strong run quality have more attacking or defensive roles?
Midfielders who have a strong run quality are best deployed in attacking roles. They can use their skills to carry the ball up field and make threatening runs in advanced areas.
What qualities do we use to evaluate ball progression in midfielders?

To evaluate ball progression we look at how well they progress the ball with passes and ball carries. We also count playmaking passes, which include progressive passes, smart passes and through passes. We look to see how much danger the midfielder creates through both passes and carrying the ball.
Does a midfielder progress the ball?
Yes, central midfielders provide an important link between defence and attack, enabling their team to move up the pitch.
What are the metric which measure if a midfielder is active defensively?

Metrics that measure if a midfielder is active defensively include their frequency of successful defensive actions and their ability to recover possession effectively. Additionally, a key indicator is their high success rate in defensive efforts.
What does it mean for a midfielder to be reliable?
Consistency in progressing the ball, creating for others and active defence are signs of reliability.
What does it mean for a player to have a high passes (xT)?
A player with a high passes (xT) is able to create a lot of expected threat from passes, and is adept at progressing the ball into more dangerous positions.
Is aerial ability important for a central midfielder?

Heading is not the most important part of a central midfielder's role. However, midfielders that are strong in the air can add value to teams by winning aeriald dules in the middle of the field and in set piece situations.
What are the metric which measure if a midfielder is intelligent defensively?

Metrics that measure if a midfielder is intelligent defensively include their frequency of successfully recovering the ball without making an active defensive action or through interceptions. Additionally, a key indicator is their ability to react quickly to the loss of possession and winning back the ball through counterpressing.
What is a midfielder?

Midfielders play in the middle of the pitch. In attack, they should move the ball from the middle of the pitch to the final third or the box. They should create chances for the wingers and forwards, but also be prepared to run in to the box or shoot when given the opportunity. Defensively, their primary job is to recover the ball in the middle of the pitch and prevent the opposition from building-up or counterattacking.
Is dribbling important for a midfielder?

Dribbling is not a key quality of midfielders, but it can be important to more creative, attacking midfielders. Midfielders who are strong dribblers can add value to their team by creating threat out of nothing by dribbling past their markers.
What makes a midfielder strong technically?

A midfielder who is good at providing teammates and progression would be defined as strong technically, demonstrating good technique on the ball. A player who is bad at providing teammates and progression would be defined as poor technically.
Why is it important to have a midfielder with high active defence?
It is important to have a midfielder with high active defence as they will be key in regaining possession of the ball, which prevents the opposition from scoring
What are the metric which measure if a midfielder has box threat?

What makes a midfielder dependable?
A dependable midfielder is a consistent performer in all important aspects of play, regardless of different tactical systems. They are above average over most metrics.
How is passing quality measured?

Passing quality is a weighted sum of a players performance compared to other players in the same position in passes (xT) (30%), crosses (xT) (20%),  passes into the final third (20 %), passes in the final third (20%) and chance passes (10%).
What qualities do we use to evaluate a midfielder?
We evaluate midfielders by their involvement, their progression, their ability to provide for teammates, their passing quality, their box threat, their active defence and their intelligent defence.
How do we measure if a midfielder provides for their teammates?

A midfielder who provides for their teammates ﻿makes a lot of key passes, assists and second assists. They will rank highly in expected goals created and expected assists. Deep completions are also important.
What are the most important metrics for a midfielder?

Ultimately, a midfielder is judged primarily on whether they control the middle section of the pitch or not. If they can move the ball forward through passes into the final third, and/or they can stop the opponent moving the ball forward, then they are doing their job well.
How is passing quality calculated?

Passing quality is calculated as the weighted sum of the z-scores of players in passes (xT) (30%), crosses (xT) (20%),  passes into the final third (20 %), passes in the final third (20%) and chance creating passes (10%), among other players who play the same position.
What does it mean for a player to have a low crosses (xT)?

A player who has a low crosses (xT) is not creating much threat from their crosses. However, they can still be dangerous passers if they rank highly in other passing xT metrics. For instance, there are many excellent chance creators who rarely cross the ball, but rather create threat from central positions.
What does it mean for a player to have bad passing quality?
Players with bad passing quality often choose safer passing options and struggle to deliver threatening passes.
What are some attributes of a midfielders with a good passing?

Midfielders who have a strong passing ability are able to make various types of dangerous passes. They can cross the ball, progress the ball into the final third and complete passes within the final third.
Would you expect a player with a high amount of chance creating passes to also have a high amount of passes (xT)?

You would expect a player with a high amount of chance creating passes to also have a high amount of passes (xT), as chance creating passes often find teammates in good positions, which inherently generate expected threat. If a player ranks highly in chance creating passes but not in passes (xT), then they are likely getting themselves into difficult positions often, and rely on their passing vision to find any teammate, even if the receiver is not in a more threatening position.
What is passing quality?

Passing quality refers to a player's ability to deliver a variety of passes that pose a significant threat to the opposition's defense, leading to goal-scoring opportunities or advantageous positions for the receiving player. It is evaluated by how threatening the passes are, rather than the quantity.
What skills would a midfielder who is less creative have in order to be considered useful to a team.

A midfielder who is weaker in terms of providing teammates can still contribute to the team if they are strong defensively or in terms of ariel duels. Some midfielders excel in defence, rather than attack. This creates stability for the team.

When a player has high passes into the final third (xT) but a low passes in the final third (xT), it may suggest that they excel in progressing the ball into dangerous areas but may not frequently participate in the final stages of the attacking build-up or goal-scoring opportunities. Their strength lies in initiating attacking moves, often creating opportunities for their teammates to take advantage of the advanced positions they help establish.
What does it indicate about a player's passing quality when they have high passes in the final third (xT) but low passes into the final third (xT)?

When a player has high passes in the final third (xT) but a low passes into the final third (xT), it suggests that they are proficient in operating within the attacking third of the field, particularly in the build-up to goal-scoring opportunities. How would we define a box-to-box midfielder?
A box-to-box midfielder is able to cover all areas of the pitch and contribute both in defence and attack. They would measure well in active defence, providing teammates and box threat.
What are the important attributes of a midfielder who has good involvement?
A midfielder is considered to have good involvement if they are active defensively, have lots of touches on the ball and are involved in play leading up to a shot.
What are important metrics for assessing a midfielder's ball progressing ability?

We would look at metrics such as progressive passes and passes into the final third, as well as using expected threat (xT) to assess their carries. Ball progression (xT) gives a good overview of these skills. If the central midfielder plays a more advanced role, they may score well for box entries too.
Are loose ball recoveries an important metric for midfielders?
Yes, the loose ball recoveries metric demonstrates how frequently a midfielder is in the right place to collect a loose ball. It gives an indication of their anticipation and positioning.
What qualities do we use to evaluate creativity in midfielders?

A midfielder who provides for their teammates is considered to be creative. These players ﻿makes a lot of key passes, assists and second assists. They will rank highly in expected goals created and expected assists. Deep completions are also important.
How would you describe a midfielder who is good in almost all metrics?
We could describe a midfielder who is good in all metrics as a well-rounded midfielder, who can contribute to the team both defensively and in attack.
What role might a midfielder who is creative have in the team?
A midfielder who is creative would usually play an attacking role, and would be given licence to move further up the pitch, to play together with the wingers and strikers to create chances.

Midfielders who have a strong passing ability are able to make various types of dangerous passes. They can cross the ball, progress the ball into the final third and complete passes within the final third.
What is passing quality?

Passing quality refers to a player's ability to deliver a variety of passes that pose a significant threat to the opposition's defense, leading to goal-scoring opportunities or advantageous positions for the receiving player. It is evaluated by how threatening the passes are, rather than the quantity.
What does it mean for a player to have good passing quality?

A midfielder who is good at creating chances would rank highly in providing teammates. They will for instance rank highly in expected goals created with passes and expected assists.

Given the definition of link-up plays, they are only counted for attacking players. Thus, they are only relevant for attacking midfielders and do not include plays where deeper midfielders receive the ball from the defenders or the goalkeeper when facing their own goal.

The primary reason teams adopt a pressing playing style is that winning the ball high up the pitch often generates threatening situations. Counterpressures are often performed after the team loses possession high up the pitch, so a successfull counterpressure usually results in an interception from that player or a teammate.

A midfielder who is good at creating chances would rank highly in providing teammates. They will for instance rank highly in expected goals created with passes and expected assists.
What is pressing?

Pressing assesses players' proactive defensive efforts to close down, pressure, or engage an opponent with the ball. It takes into account the number of defensive actions players perform, with an emphasis on counterpressing and high recoveries.

Midfielders who have a strong run quality are best deployed in attacking roles. They can use their skills to carry the ball up field and make threatening runs in advanced areas.
How is pressing  measured?

Pressing  is a weighted sum of a players performance compared to other players in the same position in defensive intensity (25%), high recoveries (35%), interceptions (10%) and counterpressing recoveries (30%).

Given the definition of link-up plays, they are only counted for attacking players. Thus, they are only relevant for attacking midfielders and do not include plays where deeper midfielders receive the ball from the defenders or the goalkeeper when facing their own goal.

A midfielder who is not above average any metrics could be described as not being a standout in any area.

Metrics that measure if a midfielder is intelligent defensively include their frequency of successfully recovering the ball without making an active defensive action or through interceptions. How would we define a box-to-box midfielder?
A box-to-box midfielder is able to cover all areas of the pitch and contribute both in defence and attack. They would measure well in active defence, providing teammates and box threat.

Heading is not the most important part of a central midfielder's role. However, midfielders that are strong in the air can add value to teams by winning aeriald dules in the middle of the field and in set piece situations.

You are the Twelve Earpiece Scout analyst. Your job is going to be to give a concise, 5 or 6 sentence summary of a midfielder's performance, specifically how it relates to aerial threat. Does a midfielder progress the ball?
Yes, central midfielders provide an important link between defence and attack, enabling their team to move up the pitch.
What are the metric which measure if a midfielder is active defensively?

Metrics that measure if a midfielder is active defensively include their frequency of successful defensive actions and their ability to recover possession effectively. Additionally, a key indicator is their high success rate in defensive efforts.
How do 'attacking aerials won' and 'attacking aerials won %' together shape a player's aerial profile in front of the goal?

Together, these aspects shape a player's aerial profile in front of the goal by highlighting their effectiveness and efficiency in offensive aerial situations, crucial for scoring or creating chances in the air.
How is aerial threat calculated?

Aerial threat is calculated as the weighted sum of the z-scores of players in aerials won (10%), aerials won % (15%), attacking aerials won (20%), attacking aerials won % (35%) and headed plays (20%), among other players who play the same position.
What makes a midfielder strong technically?

A midfielder who is good at providing teammates and progression would be defined as strong technically, demonstrating good technique on the ball. A player who is bad at providing teammates and progression would be defined as poor technically.
What are the metric which measure if a midfielder has box threat?

The key to a midfielder having high box threat is that they get in to the box with the ball and receive the balls in the penalty area. Additionally they should touch the ball alot in the box, score goals and have high expected goal shots.
What qualities do we use to evaluate a midfielder?
We evaluate midfielders by their involvement, their progression, their ability to provide for teammates, their passing quality, their box threat, their active defence and their intelligent defence.
If a midfielder is strong in attack (box threat and providing teammates) but does not rank highly in active and  intelligent defence, how do we characterise them?
A midfielder who is strong in attack but not in defence can be described as strong going forward, but at the cost of their defensive duties.
