What makes a winger strong technically?

A winger who is good in providing for their teammates and dribbling would be defined as strong technically. A winger who is bad in providing for teammates and dribbling would be defined as poor technically.
What does it mean for a player to have a high passes (xT)?
A player with a high passes (xT) is able to create a lot of expected threat from passes, and is adept at progressing the ball into more dangerous positions.

A winger with good ball retention is able to keep the ball at a high rate when they attempt dribbles. They rarely lose the ball and are trusted to receive and push the ball into dangerous and tight spaces.
What does it mean for a player to have bad passing quality?
Players with bad passing quality often choose safer passing options and struggle to deliver threatening passes.
How important is dribbling for a winger?

Dribbling can be an important attribute for a winger, as they are expected to often create threat out of nothing using their pace and technical ability. Wingers can make up for low ranking in dribbling with other skills.

What qualities do we use to evaluate a winger?
We evaluate wingers by their involvement, their passing quality, their ability to provide for teammates, their box threat, their finishing, their dribbling, their run quality and their pressing.
What can we infer from a winger that is good in terms of  run quality?
Players who rank highly in making runs tend to be faster, as they use their pace to make threatening runs and receive the ball behind the defensive line.
How is dribbling calculated?

Dribbling is calculated as the weighted sum of the z-scores of players in dribbles success % (20%), dribbles (xT) (40%), expected goals created with dribbles (25%) and pressure resistance % (15%), among other players who play the same position.
What metrics tell us that a winger is good at pressing?
A winger who presses well has lots high recoveries and makes interceptions. They have a high defence intensity and engage in counterpressing.
What can we infer from a winger that is good in both making runs and dribbling?
Players who are strong in both making runs and dribbling are likely to be faster and more agile, along with having the technical ability to carry the ball long distances and retain it.
What does it mean for a player to be bad in dribbling?
Players who are bad in dribbling either struggle to dribble past defenders or do not attempt to do so.
What does it mean for a winger to be good in ball retention?

A winger with good ball retention is able to keep the ball at a high rate when they attempt dribbles. They rarely lose the ball and are trusted to receive and push the ball into dangerous and tight spaces.
Why is dribbling not a part of run quality?

Run quality assesses the ability of players to make threatening runs without taking on players. Dribbling past players is a separate quality which is not necessarily correlated with run quality. However, the best players can do both and therefore pose a greater threat.
What are the most important metrics for a winger?

How often they contribute and are expected to contribute goals (np goals per ninety, assists per ninety, np expected goals per ninety, expected assists per ninety, chances created per ninety) as well as how good they are at running with the ball (progressive runs per ninety) are generally the most important data-points for a winger.
What are some attributes of a winger with a good run quality?

The key to a winger's run quality is making threatening runs with and without the ball and carrying the ball forward. Wingers who are good at runs take the ball into the box themselves and have a high number of penalty area receptions.
What is dribbling?

Dribbling involves the skill of taking on opposing players one-on-one. It's the ability of maneuvering the ball past defenders while maintaining control, often through quick changes in direction, feints, and close ball control.
What are some attributes of a winger with a good passing?

Wingers who have a strong passing ability are able to make various types of dangerous passes. They can cross the ball, progress the ball into the final third and complete passes within the final third.
What measurements would convince us that a winger has a high aerial threat?
A winger who wins aerial duels, who ranks highly in attacking aerials in particular is considered to have aerial threat. They will tend to head the ball a lot.
Why is it important to have a winger with a high level of pressing?

Wingers with high pressing are typically harder-working and are able to help the team's defence by spearheading their pressing attempts. They are very important to modern attacks which rely on pressing and counterpressing to win the ball back.
What can we infer from a winger who is good in providing for teammates but not ranked highly in run quality?

A winger who is good in providing for teammates but not ranked highly in run quality is selfless but does not make himself available in return. We see this happen with wingers make good passes but then hide (in that they don't find a way to receive) or don't dare to make their own runs.
What are the metric which measure if a winger has box threat?

The key to a wingers having high box threat is that they get in to the box with the ball and receive the balls in the penalty area. Additionally they should touch the ball alot in the box, score goals and have high expected goal shots.
What are the most important attributes for a winger?

There is no undeniable most important attribute for a winger. Some would argue that dribbling is most important. Others would argue that it is goal scoring and assisting. In some systems, perhaps progressing the ball and pressing is most important if they play a more reserved role.
How important is dribbling for a winger?

Dribbling can be an important attribute for a winger, as they are expected to often create threat out of nothing using their pace and technical ability. Wingers can make up for low ranking in dribbling with other skills.
What are the important metrics for a winger who is good at finishing?

The primary quality of a good finisher is that they score goals at high rate per ninety. But it is also important to look at how often they convert the chances they get and if they have high quality chances on target.
What makes a winger a strong finisher?

Wingers with excellent finishing skills tend to exhibit a notably high shot conversion percentage. Furthermore, another sign of their prowess in finishing is when they surpass their expected goals by scoring more frequently or consistently placing their shots in optimal positions, indicating a superior ability to convert opportunities compared to their expected goal values.
What are the qualities of a goal scoring winger?

The primary quality of a goal scoring winger is that they score goals at high rate per ninety. But it is also important to look at how many chances they get (even if they don't score), which we measure with the expected goals and expected goals on target per ninety metrics.
What is a winger?

A winger is the football player whose primary role is to receive the ball on the wide channels and create goal threat via dribbling, passing, and shooting.  Wingers have a variety of roles. Inverted wingers are tasked to cut-inside from the wing towards the goal and either shoot or pass. Traditional wingers are expected to dribble down the sideline before passing (or crossing) the ball into the box. In many teams, wingers have the responsibility of being one of the main creative outlets, as well as the fastest and most technically-gifted player.
What are the important attributes of a winger who has good involvement?
A winger is considered to have good involvement if they are active defensively, have lots of touches on the ball and are involved in play leading up to a shot.
What do clubs look for when scouting wingers?

Simply put, good wingers increase their team's chances of scoring a goal. This can be done in a variety of ways, such as dribbling, passing, and shooting. The best wingers in the world can do all three at a high level. Additionally, it is an added benefit if the player is both good at making runs, as well as pressing.
What makes a good dribler?
Good dribblers consistently and successfully generate threat by beating their markers in one-on-one situations. These players are typically very skillful and able to retain possession under pressure.
What does it mean for a player to be good in dribbling?

Players who are good in dribbling consistently and successfully generate threat by beating their markers in one-on-one situations. These players are typically very skillful and able to retain possession under pressure.

Dribbling is a weighted sum of a players performance compared to other players in the same position in dribbles success % (20%), dribbles (xT) (40%), expected goals created with dribbles (25%) and pressure resistance % (15%).

A good dribbling winger provides attacking threat with their dribbles. They will have a high dribbling success and have high expected threat (xT) from their dribbles. They will also have high expected goals created with dribbles, which measures whether their dribbles lead to good quality shots.

A winger who provides for their teammates ﻿makes a lot of key passes, assists and second assists. They will rank highly in expected goals created and expected assists. Deep completions are also important.
How would you describe a winger who  is good in almost all metrics?
A winger who is good in all metrics could be described as well-rounded.
What makes a winger strong technically?

A winger who is good in providing for their teammates and dribbling would be defined as strong technically. A winger who is bad in providing for teammates and dribbling would be defined as poor technically.
How would you describe a winger who is not above average in any metrics?
A winger who is not above average in any metrics could be described as not being a standout in any area.

What is a winger?

A winger is the football player whose primary role is to receive the ball on the wide channels and create goal threat via dribbling, passing, and shooting.  Wingers have a variety of roles. Inverted wingers are tasked to cut-inside from the wing towards the goal and either shoot or pass. Traditional wingers are expected to dribble down the sideline before passing (or crossing) the ball into the box. How do we measure if a winger provides for their teammates?

A winger who provides for their teammates ﻿makes a lot of key passes, assists and second assists. They will rank highly in expected goals created and expected assists. Deep completions are also important.

The primary quality of a goal scoring winger is that they score goals at high rate per ninety. But it is also important to look at how many chances they get (even if they don't score), which we measure with the expected goals and expected goals on target per ninety metrics.
What does it mean for a player to have good passing quality?

Players with good passing quality have the ability to consistently deliver different types of passes that pose a significant threat to the opposition's defense. Their passes often lead to goal-scoring opportunities or advantageous positions for their teammates.

A winger with good ball retention is able to keep the ball at a high rate when they attempt dribbles. They rarely lose the ball and are trusted to receive and push the ball into dangerous and tight spaces.

Wingers with excellent finishing skills tend to exhibit a notably high shot conversion percentage. Furthermore, another sign of their prowess in finishing is when they surpass their expected goals by scoring more frequently or consistently placing their shots in optimal positions, indicating a superior ability to convert opportunities compared to their expected goal values.
What is passing quality?

Passing quality refers to a player's ability to deliver a variety of passes that pose a significant threat to the opposition's defense, leading to goal-scoring opportunities or advantageous positions for the receiving player. It is evaluated by how threatening the passes are, rather than the quantity.
What does it mean for a player to have bad passing quality?
Players with bad passing quality often choose safer passing options and struggle to deliver threatening passes.

What metrics tell us that a winger is good at pressing?
A winger who presses well has lots high recoveries and makes interceptions. They have a high defence intensity and engage in counterpressing.
What does it mean for a player to have bad passing quality?
Players with bad passing quality often choose safer passing options and struggle to deliver threatening passes.
What are the important metrics for a winger who is good at finishing?

The primary quality of a good finisher is that they score goals at high rate per ninety. But it is also important to look at how often they convert the chances they get and if they have high quality chances on target.
What makes a winger a strong finisher?

Wingers with excellent finishing skills tend to exhibit a notably high shot conversion percentage. Furthermore, another sign of their prowess in finishing is when they surpass their expected goals by scoring more frequently or consistently placing their shots in optimal positions, indicating a superior ability to convert opportunities compared to their expected goal values.
How do we measure if a winger provides for their teammates?

A winger who provides for their teammates ﻿makes a lot of key passes, assists and second assists. They will rank highly in expected goals created and expected assists. Deep completions are also important.
What are some attributes of a winger with a good run quality?

The key to a winger's run quality is making threatening runs with and without the ball and carrying the ball forward. Wingers who are good at runs take the ball into the box themselves and have a high number of penalty area receptions.
What makes a winger strong technically?

A winger who is good in providing for their teammates and dribbling would be defined as strong technically. A winger who is bad in providing for teammates and dribbling would be defined as poor technically.
What do clubs look for when scouting wingers?

Simply put, good wingers increase their team's chances of scoring a goal. This can be done in a variety of ways, such as dribbling, passing, and shooting. The best wingers in the world can do all three at a high level. Additionally, it is an added benefit if the player is both good at making runs, as well as pressing.

A winger with good ball retention is able to keep the ball at a high rate when they attempt dribbles. They rarely lose the ball and are trusted to receive and push the ball into dangerous and tight spaces.

Passing quality is calculated as the weighted sum of the z-scores of players in passes (xT) (30%), crosses (xT) (20%),  passes into the final third (20 %), passes in the final third (20%) and chance creating passes (10%), among other players who play the same position.

Passing quality refers to a player's ability to deliver a variety of passes that pose a significant threat to the opposition's defense, leading to goal-scoring opportunities or advantageous positions for the receiving player. It is evaluated by how threatening the passes are, rather than the quantity.

How is passing quality measured?

Passing quality is a weighted sum of a players performance compared to other players in the same position in passes (xT) (30%), crosses (xT) (20%),  passes into the final third (20 %), passes in the final third (20%) and chance passes (10%).
What are some attributes of a winger with a good passing?

What are the important attributes of a winger who has good involvement?
A winger is considered to have good involvement if they are active defensively, have lots of touches on the ball and are involved in play leading up to a shot.
What metrics tell us that a winger is strong in dribbling?

What can we infer from a winger that is good in both making runs and dribbling?
Players who are strong in both making runs and dribbling are likely to be faster and more agile, along with having the technical ability to carry the ball long distances and retain it.
What does it mean for a player to have a high passes (xT)?
A player with a high passes (xT) is able to create a lot of expected threat from passes, and is adept at progressing the ball into more dangerous positions.
How would you describe a winger who is not above average in any metrics?
A winger who is not above average in any metrics could be described as not being a standout in any area.
How would you describe a winger who  is good in almost all metrics?
A winger who is good in all metrics could be described as well-rounded.

What does it mean for a player to have a low crosses (xT)?

A player who has a low crosses (xT) is not creating much threat from their crosses. However, they can still be dangerous passers if they rank highly in other passing xT metrics. What are the most important metrics for a winger?

Why is it important to have a winger with a high level of pressing?

Wingers with high pressing are typically harder-working and are able to help the team's defence by spearheading their pressing attempts. They are very important to modern attacks which rely on pressing and counterpressing to win the ball back.
What are the qualities of a goal scoring winger?

The primary quality of a goal scoring winger is that they score goals at high rate per ninety. But it is also important to look at how many chances they get (even if they don't score), which we measure with the expected goals and expected goals on target per ninety metrics.
What are the metric which measure if a winger has box threat?

The key to a wingers having high box threat is that they get in to the box with the ball and receive the balls in the penalty area. Additionally they should touch the ball alot in the box, score goals and have high expected goal shots.
What is a winger?

A winger is the football player whose primary role is to receive the ball on the wide channels and create goal threat via dribbling, passing, and shooting.  Wingers have a variety of roles. Inverted wingers are tasked to cut-inside from the wing towards the goal and either shoot or pass. Traditional wingers are expected to dribble down the sideline before passing (or crossing) the ball into the box. In many teams, wingers have the responsibility of being one of the main creative outlets, as well as the fastest and most technically-gifted player.

There is no undeniable most important attribute for a winger. Some would argue that dribbling is most important. Others would argue that it is goal scoring and assisting. In some systems, perhaps progressing the ball and pressing is most important if they play a more reserved role.
What can we infer from a winger that is good in terms of  run quality?
Players who rank highly in making runs tend to be faster, as they use their pace to make threatening runs and receive the ball behind the defensive line.
What qualities do we use to evaluate a winger?
We evaluate wingers by their involvement, their passing quality, their ability to provide for teammates, their box threat, their finishing, their dribbling, their run quality and their pressing.
How important is dribbling for a winger?

Dribbling can be an important attribute for a winger, as they are expected to often create threat out of nothing using their pace and technical ability. Wingers can make up for low ranking in dribbling with other skills.

Box threat assesses a player's ability to make an impact in and around the opposition's penalty area. It considers both the goal-scoring threat and the involvement of players inside of the penalty area.  This quality is particularly relevant for players in attacking roles.

Box threat focuses on the goal-scoring threat and involvement of players inside of the penalty are, rather than their creation. Metrics such as assists, expected assists and key passes are represented in the quality providing teammates.

Wingers with high pressing are typically harder-working and are able to help the team's defence by spearheading their pressing attempts. They are very important to modern attacks which rely on pressing and counterpressing to win the ball back.

Dribbling can be an important attribute for a winger, as they are expected to often create threat out of nothing using their pace and technical ability. Wingers can make up for low ranking in dribbling with other skills.

A winger is the football player whose primary role is to receive the ball on the wide channels and create goal threat via dribbling, passing, and shooting.  Wingers have a variety of roles. A winger is considered to have good involvement if they are active defensively, have lots of touches on the ball and are involved in play leading up to a shot.

A player with low box receptions per 90 is not a constant presence in the opposition penalty box. They are more comfortable playing deeper, possibly as a pivot or playmaker instead of a creative edge high in the midfield.

Box threat focuses on the goal-scoring threat and involvement of players inside of the penalty are, rather than their creation. Metrics such as assists, expected assists and key passes are represented in the quality providing teammates.

What is a winger?

A winger is the football player whose primary role is to receive the ball on the wide channels and create goal threat via dribbling, passing, and shooting.  Wingers have a variety of roles. Inverted wingers are tasked to cut-inside from the wing towards the goal and either shoot or pass. Traditional wingers are expected to dribble down the sideline before passing (or crossing) the ball into the box. In many teams, wingers have the responsibility of being one of the main creative outlets, as well as the fastest and most technically-gifted player.

Box threat is a weighted sum of a players performance compared to other players in the same position in touches in box (20%), box entries from carries (10%), goals (25%), expected goals (25%) and penalty area receptions (20%).
What are the most important attributes for a winger?

What does it mean for a player to have a low box threat?

How is box threat calculated?

A winger who is good in providing for their teammates and dribbling would be defined as strong technically. A winger who is bad in providing for teammates and dribbling would be defined as poor technically.
How important is dribbling for a winger?

What can we infer from a winger that is good in terms of  run quality?

How important is dribbling for a winger?

Dribbling can be an important attribute for a winger, as they are expected to often create threat out of nothing using their pace and technical ability. Wingers can make up for low ranking in dribbling with other skills.
What makes a winger a strong finisher?

Wingers with excellent finishing skills tend to exhibit a notably high shot conversion percentage. Furthermore, another sign of their prowess in finishing is when they surpass their expected goals by scoring more frequently or consistently placing their shots in optimal positions, indicating a superior ability to convert opportunities compared to their expected goal values.
What can we infer from a winger that is good in terms of  run quality?
Players who rank highly in making runs tend to be faster, as they use their pace to make threatening runs and receive the ball behind the defensive line.
What measurements would convince us that a winger has a high aerial threat?
A winger who wins aerial duels, who ranks highly in attacking aerials in particular is considered to have aerial threat. They will tend to head the ball a lot.
What can we infer from a winger who is good in providing for teammates but not ranked highly in run quality?

A winger who is good in providing for teammates but not ranked highly in run quality is selfless but does not make himself available in return. We see this happen with wingers make good passes but then hide (in that they don't find a way to receive) or don't dare to make their own runs.

We evaluate wingers by their involvement, their passing quality, their ability to provide for teammates, their box threat, their finishing, their dribbling, their run quality and their pressing.

How do we measure if a winger provides for their teammates?

What do clubs look for when scouting wingers?

Simply put, good wingers increase their team's chances of scoring a goal. This can be done in a variety of ways, such as dribbling, passing, and shooting. What are the important attributes of a winger who has good involvement?
A winger is considered to have good involvement if they are active defensively, have lots of touches on the ball and are involved in play leading up to a shot.
What are some attributes of a winger with a good run quality?

What does it mean for a winger to be good in ball retention?

A winger with good ball retention is able to keep the ball at a high rate when they attempt dribbles. They rarely lose the ball and are trusted to receive and push the ball into dangerous and tight spaces.
What can we infer from a winger that is good in both making runs and dribbling?

What are the most important attributes for a winger?

There is no undeniable most important attribute for a winger. Some would argue that dribbling is most important. Others would argue that it is goal scoring and assisting. In some systems, perhaps progressing the ball and pressing is most important if they play a more reserved role.
What is a winger?

A winger is the football player whose primary role is to receive the ball on the wide channels and create goal threat via dribbling, passing, and shooting.  Wingers have a variety of roles. Inverted wingers are tasked to cut-inside from the wing towards the goal and either shoot or pass. Traditional wingers are expected to dribble down the sideline before passing (or crossing) the ball into the box. You are the Twelve Earpiece Scout analyst. Your job is going to be to give a concise, 5 or 6 sentence summary of a winger's performance, specifically how it relates to pressing. To start off with you are going to answer a series of questions about how you evaluate the performance of a winger, both in general, and for pressing specifically. These answers show how you talk in footballing terms about the statistical descriptions of a player and pressing.  Later, you are going to be given a statistical description of a player and asked to provide a summary of that player's playing style as it relates to pressing.  It is very important then that you learn to answer, not by simply repeating back the statistical information, but by using the footballing terms you have learned to describe the player.  We will tell you when you have answered enough questions and should start to provide summaries.
What is the relationship between high recoveries and counterpressures?
Counterpressures are often performed after the team loses possession high up the pitch, so a successfull counterpressure usually results in an interception from that player or a teammate.
What are the qualities of a goal scoring winger?

The primary quality of a goal scoring winger is that they score goals at high rate per ninety. But it is also important to look at how many chances they get (even if they don't score), which we measure with the expected goals and expected goals on target per ninety metrics.
What about players that don't win the ball but participate in the press?

Pressing is a team effort and, therefore, it cannot be fully attributed to the individual. However, the current dataset does not include information about the players who contribute to the pressure but don't make a defensive action. As a result, their efforts cannot be measured.
How is pressing  measured?

Pressing  is a weighted sum of a players performance compared to other players in the same position in defensive intensity (25%), high recoveries (35%), interceptions (10%) and counterpressing recoveries (30%).
What is a winger?

A winger is the football player whose primary role is to receive the ball on the wide channels and create goal threat via dribbling, passing, and shooting.  Wingers have a variety of roles. Inverted wingers are tasked to cut-inside from the wing towards the goal and either shoot or pass. Traditional wingers are expected to dribble down the sideline before passing (or crossing) the ball into the box. In many teams, wingers have the responsibility of being one of the main creative outlets, as well as the fastest and most technically-gifted player.
How important is dribbling for a winger?

Dribbling can be an important attribute for a winger, as they are expected to often create threat out of nothing using their pace and technical ability. Wingers can make up for low ranking in dribbling with other skills.
What can we infer from a winger who is good in providing for teammates but not ranked highly in run quality?

A winger who is good in providing for teammates but not ranked highly in run quality is selfless but does not make himself available in return. We see this happen with wingers make good passes but then hide (in that they don't find a way to receive) or don't dare to make their own runs.
What metrics tell us that a winger is strong in dribbling?

A good dribbling winger provides attacking threat with their dribbles. They will have a high dribbling success and have high expected threat (xT) from their dribbles. They will also have high expected goals created with dribbles, which measures whether their dribbles lead to good quality shots.
What are the important metrics for a winger who is good at finishing?

The primary quality of a good finisher is that they score goals at high rate per ninety. But it is also important to look at how often they convert the chances they get and if they have high quality chances on target.
What are some attributes of a winger with a good passing?

Wingers who have a strong passing ability are able to make various types of dangerous passes. They can cross the ball, progress the ball into the final third and complete passes within the final third.
What are the important attributes of a winger who has good involvement?
A winger is considered to have good involvement if they are active defensively, have lots of touches on the ball and are involved in play leading up to a shot.
What is pressing?

Pressing assesses players' proactive defensive efforts to close down, pressure, or engage an opponent with the ball. It takes into account the number of defensive actions players perform, with an emphasis on counterpressing and high recoveries.
How do we measure if a winger provides for their teammates?

A winger who provides for their teammates ﻿makes a lot of key passes, assists and second assists. They will rank highly in expected goals created and expected assists. Deep completions are also important.
How would you describe a winger who  is good in almost all metrics?
A winger who is good in all metrics could be described as well-rounded.
What are the most important metrics for a winger?

How often they contribute and are expected to contribute goals (np goals per ninety, assists per ninety, np expected goals per ninety, expected assists per ninety, chances created per ninety) as well as how good they are at running with the ball (progressive runs per ninety) are generally the most important data-points for a winger.
Why is it important to have a winger with a high level of pressing?

Wingers with high pressing are typically harder-working and are able to help the team's defence by spearheading their pressing attempts. They are very important to modern attacks which rely on pressing and counterpressing to win the ball back.
What qualities do we use to evaluate a winger?
We evaluate wingers by their involvement, their passing quality, their ability to provide for teammates, their box threat, their finishing, their dribbling, their run quality and their pressing.
What does it mean for a winger to be good in ball retention?

A winger with good ball retention is able to keep the ball at a high rate when they attempt dribbles. They rarely lose the ball and are trusted to receive and push the ball into dangerous and tight spaces.
What metrics tell us that a winger is good at pressing?
A winger who presses well has lots high recoveries and makes interceptions. They have a high defence intensity and engage in counterpressing.
What does it mean for a player to have a high amount of counterpressures but low defensive intensity?

A player with a high amount of counterpressures but low defensive intensity is likely making a lot of defensive efforts immediately after their team loses possession, but overall they do not make many on ball defensive actions.
What do clubs look for when scouting wingers?

Simply put, good wingers increase their team's chances of scoring a goal. This can be done in a variety of ways, such as dribbling, passing, and shooting. The best wingers in the world can do all three at a high level. Additionally, it is an added benefit if the player is both good at making runs, as well as pressing.
What are some attributes of a winger with a good run quality?

The key to a winger's run quality is making threatening runs with and without the ball and carrying the ball forward. Wingers who are good at runs take the ball into the box themselves and have a high number of penalty area receptions.
How is pressing calculated?

Pressing is calculated as the weighted sum of the z-scores of players in defensive intensity (25%), high recoveries (35%), interceptions (10%) and counterpressing recoveries (30%), among other players who play the same position.
What makes a winger a strong finisher?

Wingers with excellent finishing skills tend to exhibit a notably high shot conversion percentage. Furthermore, another sign of their prowess in finishing is when they surpass their expected goals by scoring more frequently or consistently placing their shots in optimal positions, indicating a superior ability to convert opportunities compared to their expected goal values.
What measurements would convince us that a winger has a high aerial threat?
A winger who wins aerial duels, who ranks highly in attacking aerials in particular is considered to have aerial threat. They will tend to head the ball a lot.
How would you describe a winger who is not above average in any metrics?
A winger who is not above average in any metrics could be described as not being a standout in any area.
What makes a winger strong technically?

A winger who is good in providing for their teammates and dribbling would be defined as strong technically. A winger who is bad in providing for teammates and dribbling would be defined as poor technically.
What are the most important attributes for a winger?

There is no undeniable most important attribute for a winger. Some would argue that dribbling is most important. Others would argue that it is goal scoring and assisting. In some systems, perhaps progressing the ball and pressing is most important if they play a more reserved role.
What does it mean for a player to be bad in pressing?

Players who struggle with pressing may contribute less defensively and find it challenging to disrupt the opponent's play, which isn't solely linked to their defensive work rate, as it can result from unsuccessful efforts.
What are the metric which measure if a winger has box threat?

The key to a wingers having high box threat is that they get in to the box with the ball and receive the balls in the penalty area. Additionally they should touch the ball alot in the box, score goals and have high expected goal shots.
What does it mean for a player to rank highly in counterpressures and defensive intensity?
A player who ranks highly in counterpressures and defensive intensity has a high defensive engagement and agresssion, and has a good work rate to attempt win the ball back.
What can we infer from a winger that is good in both making runs and dribbling?
Players who are strong in both making runs and dribbling are likely to be faster and more agile, along with having the technical ability to carry the ball long distances and retain it.
What does it mean for a player to be good in pressing?
Players who are good in pressing have a high defensive work rate and are skilled in winning possession high up on the pitch, which can generate dangerous offensive transitions.
Why are high recoveries a part of pressing?

The primary reason teams adopt a pressing playing style is that winning the ball high up the pitch often generates threatening situations. Consequently, high recoveries are of great importance when measuring pressing. Equally important is contributing to the press without recovering the ball, but the current dataset lacks information about these efforts.
What can we infer from a winger that is good in terms of  run quality?
Players who rank highly in making runs tend to be faster, as they use their pace to make threatening runs and receive the ball behind the defensive line.

When a player has average defensive intensity in the attacking right half space, what does it mean?

If a player has average defensive intensity in the attacking right half-space, it means that they are quick to press opposition players in the right channels without necessarily being relentless. They are not lazy, and indeed press, but once the ball is played past them, might cool off.
How do you describe a player with outstanding defensive intensity in the defensive central midfield?

A player with outstanding defensive intensity in the defensive central midfield is the heart of the team's defensive efforts in the attacking third, showing exceptional work rate, fierce tackling, and determination to recover possession.
What does excellent defensive intensity in the defensive left wing tell us about a player?

Excellent defensive intensity in the left wing tells us that a player engages in a lot of tackles and pressures from the left back area. They are a dominant defensive presence in the team and don't let opponents go past without a fight.
How do you describe a player who has below average defensive intensity in the attacking left wing?

A player with below average defensive intensity in the attacking right wing is a right-sided wide player who barely engages with opposition full backs. They mostly let the play pass them by, only rarely getting into tackles and pressures on that side.
How do you describe a player with excellent defensive intensity in the attacking left half-space?

A player with excellent defensive intensity in the attacking left half-space is good at defending vigorously in the left channel, using their energy and tactical intelligence to disrupt the opposition's right-sided defenders any rhythm and regain control of the ball.
What does poor defensive intensity in the defensive right wing tell us about a player?

When a player has poor defensive intensity in the defensive right wing, they are quite passive when opposition attacks from their left hand side. They are probably right-sided midfielders or wingers who are somewhat lazy at tracking opposition runners and retrieving the ball.
How do you describe a player with below-average defensive intensity in the opposition penalty area?

A player with below-average defensive intensity in the opposition penalty area may not apply sufficient pressure on opposition defenders, potentially allowing them more space and time to make decisive passes, which could lead to build-up opportunities.
How do you describe a player who shows poor defensive intensity in the attacking central midfield?

A player who shows poor defensive intensity in the attacking central midfield may struggle to effectively contribute to the team's defensive shape high in the central areas. They are often being bypassed or outmaneuvered by opponents, highlighting a critical area for improvement in their overall defensive game.
How do you describe a player who has excellent defensive intensity in the attacking left wing?

A player with excellent defensive intensity in the attacking left wing is a wide player with excellent work rate. They track opposition fullbacks and defenders with vigor and engage in duels whenever possible.

You will be given a statistical description of a player's performance in terms of a metric. The description will be split up into different areas of the pitch. You must use the description enclosed in to give a concise, 2 sentence summary of the above data in footballing terms.The summary should assess both their overall ability in pressing and detail areas where they are particularly strong or weak (metrics which are average don't always need to be mentioned). You are the Twelve Earpiece Scout analyst. Your job is going to be to give a concise, 5 or 6 sentence summary of a winger's performance, specifically how it relates to aerial threat. To start off with you are going to answer a series of questions about how you evaluate the performance of a winger, both in general, and for aerial threat specifically. These answers show how you talk in footballing terms about the statistical descriptions of a player and aerial threat.  Later, you are going to be given a statistical description of a player and asked to provide a summary of that player's playing style as it relates to aerial threat.  It is very important then that you learn to answer, not by simply repeating back the statistical information, but by using the footballing terms you have learned to describe the player.  We will tell you when you have answered enough questions and should start to provide summaries.
What is a winger?

A winger is the football player whose primary role is to receive the ball on the wide channels and create goal threat via dribbling, passing, and shooting.  Wingers have a variety of roles. Inverted wingers are tasked to cut-inside from the wing towards the goal and either shoot or pass. Traditional wingers are expected to dribble down the sideline before passing (or crossing) the ball into the box. In many teams, wingers have the responsibility of being one of the main creative outlets, as well as the fastest and most technically-gifted player.
What makes a winger strong technically?

A winger who is good in providing for their teammates and dribbling would be defined as strong technically. A winger who is bad in providing for teammates and dribbling would be defined as poor technically.
What measurements would convince us that a winger has a high aerial threat?
A winger who wins aerial duels, who ranks highly in attacking aerials in particular is considered to have aerial threat. They will tend to head the ball a lot.
What are the qualities of a goal scoring winger?

The primary quality of a goal scoring winger is that they score goals at high rate per ninety. But it is also important to look at how many chances they get (even if they don't score), which we measure with the expected goals and expected goals on target per ninety metrics.
Why are aerials won a part of aerial threat?

While aerial threat primarily assesses a player's offensive danger in the air, it's important to consider their overall aerial strength. Players who consistently win aerial duels demonstrate greater aerial prowess and, consequently, a heightened aerial threat.
How important are 'attacking aerials won' for a player's aerial threat?
Attacking aerials won'  are crucial for a player, indicating their ability to win headers in offensive situations, particularly in creating scoring opportunities or directing headers on target.
How important is dribbling for a winger?

Dribbling can be an important attribute for a winger, as they are expected to often create threat out of nothing using their pace and technical ability. Wingers can make up for low ranking in dribbling with other skills.
How would you describe a winger who is not above average in any metrics?
A winger who is not above average in any metrics could be described as not being a standout in any area.
What are some attributes of a winger with a good run quality?

The key to a winger's run quality is making threatening runs with and without the ball and carrying the ball forward. Wingers who are good at runs take the ball into the box themselves and have a high number of penalty area receptions.
How is aerial threat measured?

Aerial threat is a weighted sum of a players performance compared to other players in the same position in aerials won (10%), aerials won % (15%), attacking aerials won (20%), attacking aerials won % (35%) and headed plays (20%).
What can we infer from a winger that is good in both making runs and dribbling?
Players who are strong in both making runs and dribbling are likely to be faster and more agile, along with having the technical ability to carry the ball long distances and retain it.
What are the most important attributes for a winger?

There is no undeniable most important attribute for a winger. Some would argue that dribbling is most important. Others would argue that it is goal scoring and assisting. In some systems, perhaps progressing the ball and pressing is most important if they play a more reserved role.
What does it mean for a winger to be good in ball retention?

A winger with good ball retention is able to keep the ball at a high rate when they attempt dribbles. They rarely lose the ball and are trusted to receive and push the ball into dangerous and tight spaces.
What are some attributes of a winger with a good passing?

Wingers who have a strong passing ability are able to make various types of dangerous passes. They can cross the ball, progress the ball into the final third and complete passes within the final third.
What qualities do we use to evaluate a winger?
We evaluate wingers by their involvement, their passing quality, their ability to provide for teammates, their box threat, their finishing, their dribbling, their run quality and their pressing.
How would we describe a player who is outstanding at aerial threat?
An outstanding player in this area is highly effective in winning aerial battles, arriving with good timing to balls from crosses, and contributing significantly to aerial dominance.
What does it mean for a player to have a low aerial threat?
Players who rank badly in aerial threat rarely win offensive aerial duels and usually do not pose a goal-scoring danger in the air.
What are the most important metrics for a winger?

How often they contribute and are expected to contribute goals (np goals per ninety, assists per ninety, np expected goals per ninety, expected assists per ninety, chances created per ninety) as well as how good they are at running with the ball (progressive runs per ninety) are generally the most important data-points for a winger.
What are the important attributes of a winger who has good involvement?
A winger is considered to have good involvement if they are active defensively, have lots of touches on the ball and are involved in play leading up to a shot.
What metrics tell us that a winger is good at pressing?
A winger who presses well has lots high recoveries and makes interceptions. They have a high defence intensity and engage in counterpressing.
What makes a winger a strong finisher?

Wingers with excellent finishing skills tend to exhibit a notably high shot conversion percentage. Furthermore, another sign of their prowess in finishing is when they surpass their expected goals by scoring more frequently or consistently placing their shots in optimal positions, indicating a superior ability to convert opportunities compared to their expected goal values.
What are the important metrics for a winger who is good at finishing?

The primary quality of a good finisher is that they score goals at high rate per ninety. But it is also important to look at how often they convert the chances they get and if they have high quality chances on target.
What does it mean for a player to be an aerial threat?

Players who rank highly in aerial threat are threatining in the air offensively. They win a high percentage of their aerial duels, especially in the attacking 60 % of the field, and frequently make headed passes or headed shots.
What metrics tell us that a winger is strong in dribbling?

A good dribbling winger provides attacking threat with their dribbles. They will have a high dribbling success and have high expected threat (xT) from their dribbles. They will also have high expected goals created with dribbles, which measures whether their dribbles lead to good quality shots.
Why are headed plays a part of aerial threat?

A player's ability to successfully pass the ball with their head and head the ball towards the goal is indicative of their aerial threat. It shows that they are able to control the ball with their head and to get into goal-scoring positions.
How would we describe a player who is average at aerial threat?
This player shows moderate ability in aerial challenges, occasionally winning headers but may lack consistency or physical dominance in these aerial duels.
What is aerial threat?
Aerial threat refers to a player's ability to pose a danger and get into scoring opportunities in the air, often in set-pieces.
Why is it important to have a winger with a high level of pressing?

Wingers with high pressing are typically harder-working and are able to help the team's defence by spearheading their pressing attempts. They are very important to modern attacks which rely on pressing and counterpressing to win the ball back.
How does a player's overall 'aerial threat' influence their role in set-pieces?
A player's overall 'aerial threat' directly influences their role in set-pieces. Players with high skill in aerial threat are often targeted in offensive set-pieces for headers.
What are the metric which measure if a winger has box threat?

The key to a wingers having high box threat is that they get in to the box with the ball and receive the balls in the penalty area. Additionally they should touch the ball alot in the box, score goals and have high expected goal shots.
How would you describe a winger who  is good in almost all metrics?
A winger who is good in all metrics could be described as well-rounded.
What can we infer from a winger that is good in terms of  run quality?
Players who rank highly in making runs tend to be faster, as they use their pace to make threatening runs and receive the ball behind the defensive line.
What can we infer from a winger who is good in providing for teammates but not ranked highly in run quality?

A winger who is good in providing for teammates but not ranked highly in run quality is selfless but does not make himself available in return. We see this happen with wingers make good passes but then hide (in that they don't find a way to receive) or don't dare to make their own runs.
What do clubs look for when scouting wingers?

Simply put, good wingers increase their team's chances of scoring a goal. This can be done in a variety of ways, such as dribbling, passing, and shooting. The best wingers in the world can do all three at a high level. Additionally, it is an added benefit if the player is both good at making runs, as well as pressing.
How is aerial threat calculated?

Aerial threat is calculated as the weighted sum of the z-scores of players in aerials won (10%), aerials won % (15%), attacking aerials won (20%), attacking aerials won % (35%) and headed plays (20%), among other players who play the same position.
How do we measure if a winger provides for their teammates?

A winger who provides for their teammates ﻿makes a lot of key passes, assists and second assists. They will rank highly in expected goals created and expected assists. Deep completions are also important.
How do 'attacking aerials won' and 'attacking aerials won %' together shape a player's aerial profile in front of the goal?

Together, these aspects shape a player's aerial profile in front of the goal by highlighting their effectiveness and efficiency in offensive aerial situations, crucial for scoring or creating chances in the air.

A winger who is good in providing for teammates but not ranked highly in run quality is selfless but does not make himself available in return. We see this happen with wingers make good passes but then hide (in that they don't find a way to receive) or don't dare to make their own runs.
What are the most important metrics for a winger?

How often they contribute and are expected to contribute goals (np goals per ninety, assists per ninety, np expected goals per ninety, expected assists per ninety, chances created per ninety) as well as how good they are at running with the ball (progressive runs per ninety) are generally the most important data-points for a winger.

Wingers who have a strong passing ability are able to make various types of dangerous passes. They can cross the ball, progress the ball into the final third and complete passes within the final third.

A winger who wins aerial duels, who ranks highly in attacking aerials in particular is considered to have aerial threat. They will tend to head the ball a lot.

A winger who is good in providing for their teammates and dribbling would be defined as strong technically. A winger who is bad in providing for teammates and dribbling would be defined as poor technically.

How is pressing calculated?

Pressing is calculated as the weighted sum of the z-scores of players in defensive intensity (25%), high recoveries (35%), interceptions (10%) and counterpressing recoveries (30%), among other players who play the same position.

The primary quality of a good finisher is that they score goals at high rate per ninety. But it is also important to look at how often they convert the chances they get and if they have high quality chances on target.

A winger with good ball retention is able to keep the ball at a high rate when they attempt dribbles. They rarely lose the ball and are trusted to receive and push the ball into dangerous and tight spaces.
What makes a winger a strong finisher?

Wingers with high pressing are typically harder-working and are able to help the team's defence by spearheading their pressing attempts. They are very important to modern attacks which rely on pressing and counterpressing to win the ball back.

Traditional wingers are expected to dribble down the sideline before passing (or crossing) the ball into the box. A winger is the football player whose primary role is to receive the ball on the wide channels and create goal threat via dribbling, passing, and shooting.  Wingers have a variety of roles. Inverted wingers are tasked to cut-inside from the wing towards the goal and either shoot or pass. Traditional wingers are expected to dribble down the sideline before passing (or crossing) the ball into the box. In many teams, wingers have the responsibility of being one of the main creative outlets, as well as the fastest and most technically-gifted player.

What metrics tell us that a winger is strong in dribbling?

What does it mean for a winger to be good in ball retention?

A winger with good ball retention is able to keep the ball at a high rate when they attempt dribbles. They rarely lose the ball and are trusted to receive and push the ball into dangerous and tight spaces.

A player's overall 'aerial threat' directly influences their role in set-pieces. Players with high skill in aerial threat are often targeted in offensive set-pieces for headers.

The best wingers in the world can do all three at a high level. Additionally, it is an added benefit if the player is both good at making runs, as well as pressing.
What qualities do we use to evaluate a winger?
We evaluate wingers by their involvement, their passing quality, their ability to provide for teammates, their box threat, their finishing, their dribbling, their run quality and their pressing.
What metrics tell us that a winger is good at pressing?
A winger who presses well has lots high recoveries and makes interceptions. They have a high defence intensity and engage in counterpressing.
Why is expected goals buildup a part of involvement?
Expected goals buildup is included in involvement to give higher importance to offensive actions that are part of attacks leading to shots.
What does it mean for a player to rank poorly in expected goals buildup but highly in touches?

A player who ranks poorly in expected goals buildup but highly in touches is getting on the ball, but not nessecarily getting involved in buildups that result in shots. This can be common in teams who try to build out from the back but struggle to create chances, as their team overall struggles to accumulate xG. So this is not always a fault of the individual player.
What does it mean for a player to have a high involvement?

Players with high involvement actively and frequently participate in various aspects of the game. High involvement suggests that the players have significant contributions to their team's performance.
What can we infer from a winger who is good in providing for teammates but not ranked highly in run quality?

A winger who is good in providing for teammates but not ranked highly in run quality is selfless but does not make himself available in return. We see this happen with wingers make good passes but then hide (in that they don't find a way to receive) or don't dare to make their own runs.
What are some attributes of a winger with a good passing?

Wingers who have a strong passing ability are able to make various types of dangerous passes. They can cross the ball, progress the ball into the final third and complete passes within the final third.
How would you describe a winger who  is good in almost all metrics?
A winger who is good in all metrics could be described as well-rounded.
How is involvement calculated?

Involvement is calculated as the weighted sum of the z-scores of players in aerials (15%), defensive actions (25%), touches (40 %) and expected goals buildup (20%), among other players who play the same position.
Why is it important to have a winger with a high level of pressing?

Wingers with high pressing are typically harder-working and are able to help the team's defence by spearheading their pressing attempts. They are very important to modern attacks which rely on pressing and counterpressing to win the ball back.
What is a winger?

A winger is the football player whose primary role is to receive the ball on the wide channels and create goal threat via dribbling, passing, and shooting.  Wingers have a variety of roles. Inverted wingers are tasked to cut-inside from the wing towards the goal and either shoot or pass. Traditional wingers are expected to dribble down the sideline before passing (or crossing) the ball into the box. In many teams, wingers have the responsibility of being one of the main creative outlets, as well as the fastest and most technically-gifted player.
What does it mean for a player to rank highly in expected goals buildup and touches, but poorly in defensive actions won?

A player who ranks highly in expected goals buildup and touches, but poorly in defensive actions is more involved in the team's attacking buildup, but likely doesn't contribute much defensively. This can be due to the players strengths and weaknesses, as well as the team's tactics, as perhaps this player is not responsibile to contribute often to winning the ball back if there is another player with the opposite responsibilities.
What can we infer from a winger that is good in terms of  run quality?
Players who rank highly in making runs tend to be faster, as they use their pace to make threatening runs and receive the ball behind the defensive line.
What measurements would convince us that a winger has a high aerial threat?
A winger who wins aerial duels, who ranks highly in attacking aerials in particular is considered to have aerial threat. They will tend to head the ball a lot.
What are the qualities of a goal scoring winger?

The primary quality of a goal scoring winger is that they score goals at high rate per ninety. But it is also important to look at how many chances they get (even if they don't score), which we measure with the expected goals and expected goals on target per ninety metrics.
How would we describe a player who is less involved in the game?

A player with a low involvement is less engaged in key aspects of the game, possibly contributing less to the team's overall performance and having limited influence on the tempo and structure of the match.
Why are aerials a part of involvement?

What are the most important metrics for a winger?

How would we describe a player with numerous touches across different areas of the pitch?
A player with touches across various pitch areas is versatile and heavily involved in the team’s play, contributing to both defensive and offensive phases of the game.
What are the most important attributes for a winger?

There is no undeniable most important attribute for a winger. Some would argue that dribbling is most important. Others would argue that it is goal scoring and assisting. In some systems, perhaps progressing the ball and pressing is most important if they play a more reserved role.
What does it mean for a winger to be good in ball retention?

A winger with good ball retention is able to keep the ball at a high rate when they attempt dribbles. They rarely lose the ball and are trusted to receive and push the ball into dangerous and tight spaces.
What are the important metrics for a winger who is good at finishing?

The primary quality of a good finisher is that they score goals at high rate per ninety. But it is also important to look at how often they convert the chances they get and if they have high quality chances on target.
What does it mean for a player to have a low involvement?

Players with a low involvement are not actively engaged in various aspects of the game. Players with low involvement may have limited influence on the match and contribute less to their team's performance.

How would you describe a winger who is not above average in any metrics?
A winger who is not above average in any metrics could be described as not being a standout in any area.
How important is dribbling for a winger?

Dribbling can be an important attribute for a winger, as they are expected to often create threat out of nothing using their pace and technical ability. Wingers can make up for low ranking in dribbling with other skills.
What are some attributes of a winger with a good run quality?

The key to a winger's run quality is making threatening runs with and without the ball and carrying the ball forward. Wingers who are good at runs take the ball into the box themselves and have a high number of penalty area receptions.
What are the important attributes of a winger who has good involvement?
A winger is considered to have good involvement if they are active defensively, have lots of touches on the ball and are involved in play leading up to a shot.
What makes a winger strong technically?

A winger who is good in providing for their teammates and dribbling would be defined as strong technically. A winger who is bad in providing for teammates and dribbling would be defined as poor technically.
Are players with low involvement less important to their team?

What can we infer from a winger that is good in both making runs and dribbling?
Players who are strong in both making runs and dribbling are likely to be faster and more agile, along with having the technical ability to carry the ball long distances and retain it.

What metrics do we use to evaluate heading in central defenders?

We evaluate central defender's heading both offensively and defensively. In attack we evaluate the threat that they pose in offensive aerials, whereas in defensive heading we evaluate how well they perform in aerial duels close to their own goal. We factor in how many duals they win as well as their success rate.
What does it mean for a player to have a low crosses (xT)?

A player who has a low crosses (xT) is not creating much threat from their crosses. However, they can still be dangerous passers if they rank highly in other passing xT metrics. For instance, there are many excellent chance creators who rarely cross the ball, but rather create threat from central positions.
What does it mean for a player to have a high passes (xT)?
A player with a high passes (xT) is able to create a lot of expected threat from passes, and is adept at progressing the ball into more dangerous positions.
How is passing quality measured?

Passing quality is a weighted sum of a players performance compared to other players in the same position in passes (xT) (30%), crosses (xT) (20%),  passes into the final third (20 %), passes in the final third (20%) and chance passes (10%).

We evaluate central defenders by their involvement, their progression, their composure, their aerial threat, their defensive heading, their active defence and their intelligent defence.
What are the most important quality for a central defender?

The most important quality for central defenders is their active defence, which encompasses their ability to proactively intervene the oppositions attack and recovering the possession. They will also need to be strong with aerials and defensive duels and well composed, so that they do not lose the ball in dangerous situations.
What does it mean for a player to have bad passing quality?
Players with bad passing quality often choose safer passing options and struggle to deliver threatening passes.

To evaluate ball progression we look at how well they progress the ball with passes and ball carries. Winning duels is important for central defender. It gives an insight into how well they deal with a direct opponent in an one-on-one situation. Good central defenders are both strong in duels on the ground and in the air.
Is aerial ability important for a central defender?
Heading is one of the most important part of a central defender's role. They have to duel an opposition forward in the air and are vital for defending crosses in set piece situations.

Passing quality refers to a player's ability to deliver a variety of passes that pose a significant threat to the opposition's defense, leading to goal-scoring opportunities or advantageous positions for the receiving player. A central defender is considered to have good involvement if they are active defensively, have lots of touches on the ball and are involved in the build-up of attacks ending with shots.
What is a central defender?

Central defenders play in the middle of the defence, either in a pair or trio depending on the formation deployed by the manager. Their primary role is to prevent opposition attackers from having shots, by using their skills of positioning and anticipation to help regain possession, as well as blocking shots which occur.

It is important to have a central defender with high active defence as they will be vital in regaining possession, which prevents the opposition from scoring.

What is the relationship between high recoveries and counterpressures?
Counterpressures are often performed after the team loses possession high up the pitch, so a successfull counterpressure usually results in an interception from that player or a teammate.
What does it mean for a player to be good in pressing?
Players who are good in pressing have a high defensive work rate and are skilled in winning possession high up on the pitch, which can generate dangerous offensive transitions.
What are the metric which measure if a central defender is intelligent defensively?

Metrics that measure if a central defender is intelligent defensively include their frequency of successfully recovering the ball without making an active defensive action or through interceptions. Additionally, a key indicator is their ability to react quickly to the loss of possession and winning back the ball through counterpressing.
What qualities do we use to evaluate composure in central defenders?
To evaluate the composure of central defenders we look at how well they retain possession under pressure and how often they lose the ball, especially close to their own goal.
What qualities do we use to evaluate a central defender?
We evaluate central defenders by their involvement, their progression, their composure, their aerial threat, their defensive heading, their active defence and their intelligent defence.
What does it mean for a player to have a high amount of counterpressures but low defensive intensity?

A player with a high amount of counterpressures but low defensive intensity is likely making a lot of defensive efforts immediately after their team loses possession, but overall they do not make many on ball defensive actions.
Why are high recoveries a part of pressing?

The primary reason teams adopt a pressing playing style is that winning the ball high up the pitch often generates threatening situations. Consequently, high recoveries are of great importance when measuring pressing. Equally important is contributing to the press without recovering the ball, but the current dataset lacks information about these efforts.
What is pressing?

Pressing assesses players' proactive defensive efforts to close down, pressure, or engage an opponent with the ball. It takes into account the number of defensive actions players perform, with an emphasis on counterpressing and high recoveries.
What is a central defender?

Central defenders play in the middle of the defence, either in a pair or trio depending on the formation deployed by the manager. Their primary role is to prevent opposition attackers from having shots, by using their skills of positioning and anticipation to help regain possession, as well as blocking shots which occur.
Is winning duels important for a central defender?

Winning duels is important for central defender. It gives an insight into how well they deal with a direct opponent in an one-on-one situation. Good central defenders are both strong in duels on the ground and in the air.
What does it mean for a player to rank highly in counterpressures and defensive intensity?
A player who ranks highly in counterpressures and defensive intensity has a high defensive engagement and agresssion, and has a good work rate to attempt win the ball back.
What does it mean for a player to be bad in pressing?

Players who struggle with pressing may contribute less defensively and find it challenging to disrupt the opponent's play, which isn't solely linked to their defensive work rate, as it can result from unsuccessful efforts.
What about players that don't win the ball but participate in the press?

Pressing is a team effort and, therefore, it cannot be fully attributed to the individual. However, the current dataset does not include information about the players who contribute to the pressure but don't make a defensive action. As a result, their efforts cannot be measured.
Is aerial ability important for a central defender?
Heading is one of the most important part of a central defender's role. They have to duel an opposition forward in the air and are vital for defending crosses in set piece situations.
Does a central defender progress the ball?

This depends on the tactical system used by their team. Many central defenders do progress the ball up field but those without the required passing or carrying skills will play simple passes to their teammates.
What defensive actions are important for a central defender?
We would look at defensive duels, tackles, interceptions, recoveries and clearances.

How do we measure if a central defender is an aerial threat?

If a central defender is strong in active defence but does not rank highly in progression, how do we characterise them?
A central defender who is strong in active defence but does not rank highly in progression can be described as defensively solid while offering little going forward.
How is pressing calculated?

Pressing is calculated as the weighted sum of the z-scores of players in defensive intensity (25%), high recoveries (35%), interceptions (10%) and counterpressing recoveries (30%), among other players who play the same position.
Are loose ball recoveries an important metric for central defenders?

The loose ball recoveries metric is more important for midfielders. However, it does demonstrate how frequently a player is in the right place to collect a loose ball. It gives an indication of a central defender's anticipation and positioning.
What makes a central defender strong technically?

A central defender who is good at generating expected threat from ball progression and completing playmaking passes would be defined as strong technically, as they demonstrate good technique on the ball.
What are the important attributes of a central defender who has good involvement?
A central defender is considered to have good involvement if they are active defensively, have lots of touches on the ball and are involved in the build-up of attacks ending with shots.
What does it mean for a central defender to be good in defensive heading?

A central defender who is good in defensive heading would have a strong record for aerials won in their own half. This is important as opposition sides may try to get the ball to their forwards with long high passes and crosses.
What makes a central defender dependable?
A dependable central defender is a consistent performer in all important aspects of their role regardless of different tactical systems.
What metrics do we use to evaluate heading in central defenders?

We evaluate central defender's heading both offensively and defensively. In attack we evaluate the threat that they pose in offensive aerials, whereas in defensive heading we evaluate how well they perform in aerial duels close to their own goal. We factor in how many duals they win as well as their success rate.
What qualities do we use to evaluate ball progression in central defenders?

To evaluate ball progression we look at how well they progress the ball with passes and ball carries. We also count playmaking passes, which include progressive passes, smart passes and through passes. We look to see how much danger the central defender creates through both passes and carrying the ball.
What does it mean for a central defender to be reliable?
Consistent high performance in active defence, defensive heading and composure are signs of reliability for a central defender
What are the most important quality for a central defender?

The most important quality for central defenders is their active defence, which encompasses their ability to proactively intervene the oppositions attack and recovering the possession. Heading is one of the most important part of a central defender's role. They have to duel an opposition forward in the air and are vital for defending crosses in set piece situations.

To evaluate the composure of central defenders we look at how well they retain possession under pressure and how often they lose the ball, especially close to their own goal.

You are the Twelve Earpiece Scout analyst.  Your job is going to be to give a concise, 5 or 6 sentence summary of a striker's playing style, strengths and weaknesses.  To start off with you are going to answer a series of questions about how you evaluate the performance of a striker.
