What role might a midfielder who is creative have in the team?
A midfielder who is creative would usually play an attacking role, and would be given licence to move further up the pitch, to play together with the wingers and strikers to create chances.
What are the important attributes of a midfielder who has good involvement?
A midfielder is considered to have good involvement if they are active defensively, have lots of touches on the ball and are involved in play leading up to a shot.
What qualities do we use to evaluate ball progression in midfielders?

To evaluate ball progression we look at how well they progress the ball with passes and ball carries. We also count playmaking passes, which include progressive passes, smart passes and through passes. We look to see how much danger the midfielder creates through both passes and carrying the ball.
What are important metrics for assessing a midfielder's ball progressing ability?

We would look at metrics such as progressive passes and passes into the final third, as well as using expected threat (xT) to assess their carries. Ball progression (xT) gives a good overview of these skills. If the central midfielder plays a more advanced role, they may score well for box entries too.
What are the metric which measure if a midfielder has box threat?

The key to a midfielder having high box threat is that they get in to the box with the ball and receive the balls in the penalty area. Additionally they should touch the ball alot in the box, score goals and have high expected goal shots.
What is a midfielder?

Midfielders play in the middle of the pitch. In attack, they should move the ball from the middle of the pitch to the final third or the box. They should create chances for the wingers and forwards, but also be prepared to run in to the box or shoot when given the opportunity. Defensively, their primary job is to recover the ball in the middle of the pitch and prevent the opposition from building-up or counterattacking.
Should midfielders who have strong run quality have more attacking or defensive roles?
Midfielders who have a strong run quality are best deployed in attacking roles. They can use their skills to carry the ball up field and make threatening runs in advanced areas.
What are the metric which measure if a midfielder is active defensively?

Metrics that measure if a midfielder is active defensively include their frequency of successful defensive actions and their ability to recover possession effectively. Additionally, a key indicator is their high success rate in defensive efforts.
What makes a midfielder dependable?
A dependable midfielder is a consistent performer in all important aspects of play, regardless of different tactical systems. They are above average over most metrics.
What would lead us to believe that a midfielder is good at creating chances for their teammates?
A midfielder who is good at creating chances would rank highly in providing teammates. They will for instance rank highly in expected goals created with passes and expected assists.
What makes a midfielder strong technically?

A midfielder who is good at providing teammates and progression would be defined as strong technically, demonstrating good technique on the ball. A player who is bad at providing teammates and progression would be defined as poor technically.
Are loose ball recoveries an important metric for midfielders?
Yes, the loose ball recoveries metric demonstrates how frequently a midfielder is in the right place to collect a loose ball. It gives an indication of their anticipation and positioning.
How do we measure if a midfielder provides for their teammates?

A midfielder who provides for their teammates ﻿makes a lot of key passes, assists and second assists. They will rank highly in expected goals created and expected assists. Deep completions are also important.
Why is it important to have a midfielder with high active defence?
It is important to have a midfielder with high active defence as they will be key in regaining possession of the ball, which prevents the opposition from scoring
What are some attributes of a midfielders with a good passing?

Midfielders who have a strong passing ability are able to make various types of dangerous passes. They can cross the ball, progress the ball into the final third and complete passes within the final third.
How would we define a box-to-box midfielder?
A box-to-box midfielder is able to cover all areas of the pitch and contribute both in defence and attack. They would measure well in active defence, providing teammates and box threat.
If a midfielder is strong in attack (box threat and providing teammates) but does not rank highly in active and  intelligent defence, how do we characterise them?
A midfielder who is strong in attack but not in defence can be described as strong going forward, but at the cost of their defensive duties.
What qualities do we use to evaluate a midfielder?
We evaluate midfielders by their involvement, their progression, their ability to provide for teammates, their passing quality, their box threat, their active defence and their intelligent defence.
What are the metric which measure if a midfielder is intelligent defensively?

Metrics that measure if a midfielder is intelligent defensively include their frequency of successfully recovering the ball without making an active defensive action or through interceptions. Additionally, a key indicator is their ability to react quickly to the loss of possession and winning back the ball through counterpressing.
Does a midfielder progress the ball?
Yes, central midfielders provide an important link between defence and attack, enabling their team to move up the pitch.
How would you describe a midfielder who is good in almost all metrics?
We could describe a midfielder who is good in all metrics as a well-rounded midfielder, who can contribute to the team both defensively and in attack.
How would you describe a midfielder who is not above average in any metrics?
A midfielder who is not above average any metrics could be described as not being a standout in any area.
Are linkup-plays important for a midfielder?

Given the definition of link-up plays, they are only counted for attacking players. Thus, they are only relevant for attacking midfielders and do not include plays where deeper midfielders receive the ball from the defenders or the goalkeeper when facing their own goal.
What are the most important metrics for a midfielder?

Ultimately, a midfielder is judged primarily on whether they control the middle section of the pitch or not. If they can move the ball forward through passes into the final third, and/or they can stop the opponent moving the ball forward, then they are doing their job well.
What does it mean for a midfielder to be reliable?
Consistency in progressing the ball, creating for others and active defence are signs of reliability.
What qualities do we use to evaluate creativity in midfielders?

A midfielder who provides for their teammates is considered to be creative. These players ﻿makes a lot of key passes, assists and second assists. They will rank highly in expected goals created and expected assists. Deep completions are also important.
Is dribbling important for a midfielder?

Dribbling is not a key quality of midfielders, but it can be important to more creative, attacking midfielders. Midfielders who are strong dribblers can add value to their team by creating threat out of nothing by dribbling past their markers.
What skills would a midfielder who is less creative have in order to be considered useful to a team.

A midfielder who is weaker in terms of providing teammates can still contribute to the team if they are strong defensively or in terms of ariel duels. Some midfielders excel in defence, rather than attack. This creates stability for the team.
Is aerial ability important for a central midfielder?

Heading is not the most important part of a central midfielder's role. However, midfielders that are strong in the air can add value to teams by winning aeriald dules in the middle of the field and in set piece situations.

Metrics that measure if a midfielder is intelligent defensively include their frequency of successfully recovering the ball without making an active defensive action or through interceptions. A midfielder who is strong in attack but not in defence can be described as strong going forward, but at the cost of their defensive duties.

A midfielder who is good at providing teammates and progression would be defined as strong technically, demonstrating good technique on the ball. A player who is bad at providing teammates and progression would be defined as poor technically.
Should midfielders who have strong run quality have more attacking or defensive roles?
Midfielders who have a strong run quality are best deployed in attacking roles. They can use their skills to carry the ball up field and make threatening runs in advanced areas.

A dependable midfielder is a consistent performer in all important aspects of play, regardless of different tactical systems. They are above average over most metrics.

What qualities do we use to evaluate ball progression in midfielders?

What is a midfielder?

Midfielders play in the middle of the pitch. In attack, they should move the ball from the middle of the pitch to the final third or the box. A midfielder is considered to have good involvement if they are active defensively, have lots of touches on the ball and are involved in play leading up to a shot.

You are the Twelve Earpiece Scout analyst. Your job is going to be to give a concise, 5 or 6 sentence summary of a midfielder's performance, specifically how it relates to dribbling. If a midfielder is strong in attack (box threat and providing teammates) but does not rank highly in active and  intelligent defence, how do we characterise them?
A midfielder who is strong in attack but not in defence can be described as strong going forward, but at the cost of their defensive duties.
What are the most important metrics for a midfielder?

Ultimately, a midfielder is judged primarily on whether they control the middle section of the pitch or not. If they can move the ball forward through passes into the final third, and/or they can stop the opponent moving the ball forward, then they are doing their job well.
Does a midfielder progress the ball?
Yes, central midfielders provide an important link between defence and attack, enabling their team to move up the pitch.
How would you describe a midfielder who is not above average in any metrics?
A midfielder who is not above average any metrics could be described as not being a standout in any area.
Is dribbling important for a midfielder?

Dribbling is not a key quality of midfielders, but it can be important to more creative, attacking midfielders. Midfielders who are strong dribblers can add value to their team by creating threat out of nothing by dribbling past their markers.
What does it mean for a midfielder to be reliable?
Consistency in progressing the ball, creating for others and active defence are signs of reliability.
What qualities do we use to evaluate ball progression in midfielders?

To evaluate ball progression we look at how well they progress the ball with passes and ball carries. We also count playmaking passes, which include progressive passes, smart passes and through passes. We look to see how much danger the midfielder creates through both passes and carrying the ball.
What is a midfielder?

Midfielders play in the middle of the pitch. In attack, they should move the ball from the middle of the pitch to the final third or the box. They should create chances for the wingers and forwards, but also be prepared to run in to the box or shoot when given the opportunity. Defensively, their primary job is to recover the ball in the middle of the pitch and prevent the opposition from building-up or counterattacking.
What are the metric which measure if a midfielder has box threat?

The key to a midfielder having high box threat is that they get in to the box with the ball and receive the balls in the penalty area. Additionally they should touch the ball alot in the box, score goals and have high expected goal shots.
Why is it important to have a midfielder with high active defence?
It is important to have a midfielder with high active defence as they will be key in regaining possession of the ball, which prevents the opposition from scoring
Are loose ball recoveries an important metric for midfielders?
Yes, the loose ball recoveries metric demonstrates how frequently a midfielder is in the right place to collect a loose ball. It gives an indication of their anticipation and positioning.
How is dribbling measured?

Dribbling is a weighted sum of a players performance compared to other players in the same position in dribbles success % (20%), dribbles (xT) (40%), expected goals created with dribbles (25%) and pressure resistance % (15%).
What makes a midfielder dependable?
A dependable midfielder is a consistent performer in all important aspects of play, regardless of different tactical systems. They are above average over most metrics.
What does it mean for a player to be good in dribbling?

Players who are good in dribbling consistently and successfully generate threat by beating their markers in one-on-one situations. These players are typically very skillful and able to retain possession under pressure.
Are linkup-plays important for a midfielder?

Given the definition of link-up plays, they are only counted for attacking players. Thus, they are only relevant for attacking midfielders and do not include plays where deeper midfielders receive the ball from the defenders or the goalkeeper when facing their own goal.
How would we define a box-to-box midfielder?
A box-to-box midfielder is able to cover all areas of the pitch and contribute both in defence and attack. They would measure well in active defence, providing teammates and box threat.
How would you describe a midfielder who is good in almost all metrics?
We could describe a midfielder who is good in all metrics as a well-rounded midfielder, who can contribute to the team both defensively and in attack.
What are important metrics for assessing a midfielder's ball progressing ability?

We would look at metrics such as progressive passes and passes into the final third, as well as using expected threat (xT) to assess their carries. Ball progression (xT) gives a good overview of these skills. If the central midfielder plays a more advanced role, they may score well for box entries too.
What does it mean for a player to be bad in dribbling?
Players who are bad in dribbling either struggle to dribble past defenders or do not attempt to do so.
How is dribbling calculated?

Dribbling is calculated as the weighted sum of the z-scores of players in dribbles success % (20%), dribbles (xT) (40%), expected goals created with dribbles (25%) and pressure resistance % (15%), among other players who play the same position.
What qualities do we use to evaluate creativity in midfielders?

A midfielder who provides for their teammates is considered to be creative. These players ﻿makes a lot of key passes, assists and second assists. They will rank highly in expected goals created and expected assists. Deep completions are also important.
What are the metric which measure if a midfielder is active defensively?

Metrics that measure if a midfielder is active defensively include their frequency of successful defensive actions and their ability to recover possession effectively. Additionally, a key indicator is their high success rate in defensive efforts.
Should midfielders who have strong run quality have more attacking or defensive roles?
Midfielders who have a strong run quality are best deployed in attacking roles. They can use their skills to carry the ball up field and make threatening runs in advanced areas.
Is aerial ability important for a central midfielder?

Heading is not the most important part of a central midfielder's role. However, midfielders that are strong in the air can add value to teams by winning aeriald dules in the middle of the field and in set piece situations.
What would lead us to believe that a midfielder is good at creating chances for their teammates?
A midfielder who is good at creating chances would rank highly in providing teammates. They will for instance rank highly in expected goals created with passes and expected assists.
What role might a midfielder who is creative have in the team?
A midfielder who is creative would usually play an attacking role, and would be given licence to move further up the pitch, to play together with the wingers and strikers to create chances.
What are the important attributes of a midfielder who has good involvement?
A midfielder is considered to have good involvement if they are active defensively, have lots of touches on the ball and are involved in play leading up to a shot.
What are some attributes of a midfielders with a good passing?

Midfielders who have a strong passing ability are able to make various types of dangerous passes. They can cross the ball, progress the ball into the final third and complete passes within the final third.
Why is dribbling not a part of run quality?

Run quality assesses the ability of players to make threatening runs without taking on players. Dribbling past players is a separate quality which is not necessarily correlated with run quality. However, the best players can do both and therefore pose a greater threat.
What is dribbling?

Dribbling involves the skill of taking on opposing players one-on-one. It's the ability of maneuvering the ball past defenders while maintaining control, often through quick changes in direction, feints, and close ball control.
How do we measure if a midfielder provides for their teammates?

A midfielder who provides for their teammates ﻿makes a lot of key passes, assists and second assists. They will rank highly in expected goals created and expected assists. Deep completions are also important.
What makes a midfielder strong technically?

A midfielder who is good at providing teammates and progression would be defined as strong technically, demonstrating good technique on the ball. A player who is bad at providing teammates and progression would be defined as poor technically.
What qualities do we use to evaluate a midfielder?
We evaluate midfielders by their involvement, their progression, their ability to provide for teammates, their passing quality, their box threat, their active defence and their intelligent defence.
What skills would a midfielder who is less creative have in order to be considered useful to a team.

A midfielder who is weaker in terms of providing teammates can still contribute to the team if they are strong defensively or in terms of ariel duels. Some midfielders excel in defence, rather than attack. This creates stability for the team.
What are the metric which measure if a midfielder is intelligent defensively?

Metrics that measure if a midfielder is intelligent defensively include their frequency of successfully recovering the ball without making an active defensive action or through interceptions. Additionally, a key indicator is their ability to react quickly to the loss of possession and winning back the ball through counterpressing.
What makes a good dribler?
Good dribblers consistently and successfully generate threat by beating their markers in one-on-one situations. These players are typically very skillful and able to retain possession under pressure.

What makes a midfielder strong technically?

A midfielder who is good at providing teammates and progression would be defined as strong technically, demonstrating good technique on the ball. A player who is bad at providing teammates and progression would be defined as poor technically.
Does a midfielder progress the ball?
Yes, central midfielders provide an important link between defence and attack, enabling their team to move up the pitch.
What does it mean for a midfielder to be reliable?
Consistency in progressing the ball, creating for others and active defence are signs of reliability.

Dribbling is not a key quality of midfielders, but it can be important to more creative, attacking midfielders. Midfielders who are strong dribblers can add value to their team by creating threat out of nothing by dribbling past their markers.

Yes, the loose ball recoveries metric demonstrates how frequently a midfielder is in the right place to collect a loose ball. It gives an indication of their anticipation and positioning.

Dribbling involves the skill of taking on opposing players one-on-one. It's the ability of maneuvering the ball past defenders while maintaining control, often through quick changes in direction, feints, and close ball control.

Players who are good in dribbling consistently and successfully generate threat by beating their markers in one-on-one situations. These players are typically very skillful and able to retain possession under pressure.

What qualities do we use to evaluate a midfielder?

What are the most important metrics for a midfielder?

Ultimately, a midfielder is judged primarily on whether they control the middle section of the pitch or not. If they can move the ball forward through passes into the final third, and/or they can stop the opponent moving the ball forward, then they are doing their job well.

Midfielders who have a strong run quality are best deployed in attacking roles. They can use their skills to carry the ball up field and make threatening runs in advanced areas.

Metrics that measure if a midfielder is intelligent defensively include their frequency of successfully recovering the ball without making an active defensive action or through interceptions. How is dribbling calculated?

It is important to have a midfielder with high active defence as they will be key in regaining possession of the ball, which prevents the opposition from scoring

Good dribblers consistently and successfully generate threat by beating their markers in one-on-one situations. These players are typically very skillful and able to retain possession under pressure.

How would we define a box-to-box midfielder?
A box-to-box midfielder is able to cover all areas of the pitch and contribute both in defence and attack. They would measure well in active defence, providing teammates and box threat.

Midfielders play in the middle of the pitch. In attack, they should move the ball from the middle of the pitch to the final third or the box. Metrics that measure if a midfielder is active defensively include their frequency of successful defensive actions and their ability to recover possession effectively. Additionally, a key indicator is their high success rate in defensive efforts.
Does a midfielder progress the ball?

A midfielder who is creative would usually play an attacking role, and would be given licence to move further up the pitch, to play together with the wingers and strikers to create chances.

A midfielder who is good at providing teammates and progression would be defined as strong technically, demonstrating good technique on the ball. A player who is bad at providing teammates and progression would be defined as poor technically.

To evaluate ball progression we look at how well they progress the ball with passes and ball carries. We also count playmaking passes, which include progressive passes, smart passes and through passes. We look to see how much danger the midfielder creates through both passes and carrying the ball.

Box threat focuses on the goal-scoring threat and involvement of players inside of the penalty are, rather than their creation. Metrics such as assists, expected assists and key passes are represented in the quality providing teammates.

We evaluate midfielders by their involvement, their progression, their ability to provide for teammates, their passing quality, their box threat, their active defence and their intelligent defence.

The loose ball recoveries metric is more important for midfielders. However, it does demonstrate how frequently a player is in the right place to collect a loose ball. It gives an indication of a central defender's anticipation and positioning.
What qualities do we use to evaluate a central defender?
We evaluate central defenders by their involvement, their progression, their composure, their aerial threat, their defensive heading, their active defence and their intelligent defence.
What qualities do we use to evaluate ball progression in midfielders?

To evaluate ball progression we look at how well they progress the ball with passes and ball carries. We also count playmaking passes, which include progressive passes, smart passes and through passes. We look to see how much danger the midfielder creates through both passes and carrying the ball.
What is a central defender?

Central defenders play in the middle of the defence, either in a pair or trio depending on the formation deployed by the manager. Their primary role is to prevent opposition attackers from having shots, by using their skills of positioning and anticipation to help regain possession, as well as blocking shots which occur.
What are the metric which measure if a midfielder is active defensively?

Metrics that measure if a midfielder is active defensively include their frequency of successful defensive actions and their ability to recover possession effectively. Additionally, a key indicator is their high success rate in defensive efforts.

Yes, central midfielders provide an important link between defence and attack, enabling their team to move up the pitch.

Heading is not the most important part of a central midfielder's role. However, midfielders that are strong in the air can add value to teams by winning aeriald dules in the middle of the field and in set piece situations.

Players who rank badly in aerial threat rarely win offensive aerial duels and usually do not pose a goal-scoring danger in the air.
How would you describe a midfielder who is good in almost all metrics?
We could describe a midfielder who is good in all metrics as a well-rounded midfielder, who can contribute to the team both defensively and in attack.

A midfielder who is weaker in terms of providing teammates can still contribute to the team if they are strong defensively or in terms of ariel duels. Some midfielders excel in defence, rather than attack. This creates stability for the team.

Attacking aerials won'  are crucial for a player, indicating their ability to win headers in offensive situations, particularly in creating scoring opportunities or directing headers on target.

Players who rank highly in aerial threat are threatining in the air offensively. They win a high percentage of their aerial duels, especially in the attacking 60 % of the field, and frequently make headed passes or headed shots.

What are the metric which measure if a midfielder is intelligent defensively?

How would we describe a player who is outstanding at aerial threat?

We evaluate midfielders by their involvement, their progression, their ability to provide for teammates, their passing quality, their box threat, their active defence and their intelligent defence.

What are the metric which measure if a winger has box threat?

The key to a wingers having high box threat is that they get in to the box with the ball and receive the balls in the penalty area. Additionally they should touch the ball alot in the box, score goals and have high expected goal shots.

How important is dribbling for a winger?

What do clubs look for when scouting wingers?

How would you describe a winger who  is good in almost all metrics?

What can we infer from a winger that is good in terms of  run quality?

What are the most important attributes for a winger?

There is no undeniable most important attribute for a winger. Some would argue that dribbling is most important. Others would argue that it is goal scoring and assisting. In some systems, perhaps progressing the ball and pressing is most important if they play a more reserved role.
What are some attributes of a winger with a good passing?

Wingers who have a strong passing ability are able to make various types of dangerous passes. They can cross the ball, progress the ball into the final third and complete passes within the final third.
What measurements would convince us that a winger has a high aerial threat?
A winger who wins aerial duels, who ranks highly in attacking aerials in particular is considered to have aerial threat. They will tend to head the ball a lot.
What are the important metrics for a winger who is good at finishing?

The primary quality of a good finisher is that they score goals at high rate per ninety. But it is also important to look at how often they convert the chances they get and if they have high quality chances on target.
What are the most important metrics for a winger?

How often they contribute and are expected to contribute goals (np goals per ninety, assists per ninety, np expected goals per ninety, expected assists per ninety, chances created per ninety) as well as how good they are at running with the ball (progressive runs per ninety) are generally the most important data-points for a winger.
How do we measure if a winger provides for their teammates?

A winger who provides for their teammates ﻿makes a lot of key passes, assists and second assists. They will rank highly in expected goals created and expected assists. Deep completions are also important.
What are the important attributes of a winger who has good involvement?
A winger is considered to have good involvement if they are active defensively, have lots of touches on the ball and are involved in play leading up to a shot.
What are some attributes of a winger with a good run quality?

The key to a winger's run quality is making threatening runs with and without the ball and carrying the ball forward. Wingers who are good at runs take the ball into the box themselves and have a high number of penalty area receptions.
Why is it important to have a winger with a high level of pressing?

Wingers with high pressing are typically harder-working and are able to help the team's defence by spearheading their pressing attempts. They are very important to modern attacks which rely on pressing and counterpressing to win the ball back.

We evaluate wingers by their involvement, their passing quality, their ability to provide for teammates, their box threat, their finishing, their dribbling, their run quality and their pressing.

What does it mean for a player to have a high passes (xT)?
A player with a high passes (xT) is able to create a lot of expected threat from passes, and is adept at progressing the ball into more dangerous positions.

When a player has high passes into the final third (xT) but a low passes in the final third (xT), it may suggest that they excel in progressing the ball into dangerous areas but may not frequently participate in the final stages of the attacking build-up or goal-scoring opportunities. Their strength lies in initiating attacking moves, often creating opportunities for their teammates to take advantage of the advanced positions they help establish.

A winger who is good in providing for teammates but not ranked highly in run quality is selfless but does not make himself available in return. We see this happen with wingers make good passes but then hide (in that they don't find a way to receive) or don't dare to make their own runs.
What qualities do we use to evaluate a winger?
We evaluate wingers by their involvement, their passing quality, their ability to provide for teammates, their box threat, their finishing, their dribbling, their run quality and their pressing.
Why is it important to have a winger with a high level of pressing?

Wingers with high pressing are typically harder-working and are able to help the team's defence by spearheading their pressing attempts. They are very important to modern attacks which rely on pressing and counterpressing to win the ball back.
What measurements would convince us that a winger has a high aerial threat?

How is passing quality calculated?

Passing quality is calculated as the weighted sum of the z-scores of players in passes (xT) (30%), crosses (xT) (20%),  passes into the final third (20 %), passes in the final third (20%) and chance creating passes (10%), among other players who play the same position.
What metrics tell us that a winger is good at pressing?

What can we infer from a winger that is good in terms of  run quality?

What does it mean for a player to have good passing quality?

What is a winger?

A winger is the football player whose primary role is to receive the ball on the wide channels and create goal threat via dribbling, passing, and shooting.  Wingers have a variety of roles. Inverted wingers are tasked to cut-inside from the wing towards the goal and either shoot or pass. Traditional wingers are expected to dribble down the sideline before passing (or crossing) the ball into the box. In many teams, wingers have the responsibility of being one of the main creative outlets, as well as the fastest and most technically-gifted player.
What is passing quality?

Passing quality refers to a player's ability to deliver a variety of passes that pose a significant threat to the opposition's defense, leading to goal-scoring opportunities or advantageous positions for the receiving player. It is evaluated by how threatening the passes are, rather than the quantity.
What are the most important attributes for a winger?

What are the qualities of a goal scoring winger?

The primary quality of a goal scoring winger is that they score goals at high rate per ninety. But it is also important to look at how many chances they get (even if they don't score), which we measure with the expected goals and expected goals on target per ninety metrics.
What are the metric which measure if a winger has box threat?

The key to a wingers having high box threat is that they get in to the box with the ball and receive the balls in the penalty area. Additionally they should touch the ball alot in the box, score goals and have high expected goal shots.
Would you expect a player with a high amount of chance creating passes to also have a high amount of passes (xT)?

You would expect a player with a high amount of chance creating passes to also have a high amount of passes (xT), as chance creating passes often find teammates in good positions, which inherently generate expected threat. If a player ranks highly in chance creating passes but not in passes (xT), then they are likely getting themselves into difficult positions often, and rely on their passing vision to find any teammate, even if the receiver is not in a more threatening position.

Wingers with excellent finishing skills tend to exhibit a notably high shot conversion percentage. A winger who is not above average in any metrics could be described as not being a standout in any area.

A winger with good ball retention is able to keep the ball at a high rate when they attempt dribbles. They rarely lose the ball and are trusted to receive and push the ball into dangerous and tight spaces.
What are the important attributes of a winger who has good involvement?
A winger is considered to have good involvement if they are active defensively, have lots of touches on the ball and are involved in play leading up to a shot.
How important is dribbling for a winger?

Dribbling can be an important attribute for a winger, as they are expected to often create threat out of nothing using their pace and technical ability. Wingers can make up for low ranking in dribbling with other skills.
What does it mean for a player to have bad passing quality?
Players with bad passing quality often choose safer passing options and struggle to deliver threatening passes.

The primary quality of a good finisher is that they score goals at high rate per ninety. But it is also important to look at how often they convert the chances they get and if they have high quality chances on target.

A winger who is good in providing for their teammates and dribbling would be defined as strong technically. A winger who is bad in providing for teammates and dribbling would be defined as poor technically.

You are the Twelve Earpiece Scout analyst. Your job is going to be to give a concise, 5 or 6 sentence summary of a winger's performance, specifically how it relates to dribbling. To start off with you are going to answer a series of questions about how you evaluate the performance of a winger, both in general, and for dribbling specifically. These answers show how you talk in footballing terms about the statistical descriptions of a player and dribbling.  Later, you are going to be given a statistical description of a player and asked to provide a summary of that player's playing style as it relates to dribbling.  It is very important then that you learn to answer, not by simply repeating back the statistical information, but by using the footballing terms you have learned to describe the player.  We will tell you when you have answered enough questions and should start to provide summaries.
What is a winger?

A winger is the football player whose primary role is to receive the ball on the wide channels and create goal threat via dribbling, passing, and shooting.  Wingers have a variety of roles. Inverted wingers are tasked to cut-inside from the wing towards the goal and either shoot or pass. Traditional wingers are expected to dribble down the sideline before passing (or crossing) the ball into the box. In many teams, wingers have the responsibility of being one of the main creative outlets, as well as the fastest and most technically-gifted player.
How important is dribbling for a winger?

Dribbling can be an important attribute for a winger, as they are expected to often create threat out of nothing using their pace and technical ability. Wingers can make up for low ranking in dribbling with other skills.
What are some attributes of a winger with a good run quality?

The key to a winger's run quality is making threatening runs with and without the ball and carrying the ball forward. Wingers who are good at runs take the ball into the box themselves and have a high number of penalty area receptions.
How is dribbling measured?

Dribbling is a weighted sum of a players performance compared to other players in the same position in dribbles success % (20%), dribbles (xT) (40%), expected goals created with dribbles (25%) and pressure resistance % (15%).
What makes a winger a strong finisher?

Wingers with excellent finishing skills tend to exhibit a notably high shot conversion percentage. Furthermore, another sign of their prowess in finishing is when they surpass their expected goals by scoring more frequently or consistently placing their shots in optimal positions, indicating a superior ability to convert opportunities compared to their expected goal values.
What are the important metrics for a winger who is good at finishing?

The primary quality of a good finisher is that they score goals at high rate per ninety. But it is also important to look at how often they convert the chances they get and if they have high quality chances on target.
What does it mean for a player to be bad in dribbling?
Players who are bad in dribbling either struggle to dribble past defenders or do not attempt to do so.
Why is it important to have a winger with a high level of pressing?

Wingers with high pressing are typically harder-working and are able to help the team's defence by spearheading their pressing attempts. They are very important to modern attacks which rely on pressing and counterpressing to win the ball back.
What do clubs look for when scouting wingers?

Simply put, good wingers increase their team's chances of scoring a goal. This can be done in a variety of ways, such as dribbling, passing, and shooting. The best wingers in the world can do all three at a high level. Additionally, it is an added benefit if the player is both good at making runs, as well as pressing.
What makes a good dribler?
Good dribblers consistently and successfully generate threat by beating their markers in one-on-one situations. These players are typically very skillful and able to retain possession under pressure.
What are the most important attributes for a winger?

There is no undeniable most important attribute for a winger. Some would argue that dribbling is most important. Others would argue that it is goal scoring and assisting. In some systems, perhaps progressing the ball and pressing is most important if they play a more reserved role.
What is dribbling?

Dribbling involves the skill of taking on opposing players one-on-one. It's the ability of maneuvering the ball past defenders while maintaining control, often through quick changes in direction, feints, and close ball control.
What can we infer from a winger that is good in both making runs and dribbling?
Players who are strong in both making runs and dribbling are likely to be faster and more agile, along with having the technical ability to carry the ball long distances and retain it.
What does it mean for a player to be good in dribbling?

Players who are good in dribbling consistently and successfully generate threat by beating their markers in one-on-one situations. These players are typically very skillful and able to retain possession under pressure.
What can we infer from a winger who is good in providing for teammates but not ranked highly in run quality?

A winger who is good in providing for teammates but not ranked highly in run quality is selfless but does not make himself available in return. We see this happen with wingers make good passes but then hide (in that they don't find a way to receive) or don't dare to make their own runs.
What measurements would convince us that a winger has a high aerial threat?
A winger who wins aerial duels, who ranks highly in attacking aerials in particular is considered to have aerial threat. They will tend to head the ball a lot.
What does it mean for a winger to be good in ball retention?

A winger with good ball retention is able to keep the ball at a high rate when they attempt dribbles. They rarely lose the ball and are trusted to receive and push the ball into dangerous and tight spaces.
How would you describe a winger who  is good in almost all metrics?
A winger who is good in all metrics could be described as well-rounded.
How is dribbling calculated?

Dribbling is calculated as the weighted sum of the z-scores of players in dribbles success % (20%), dribbles (xT) (40%), expected goals created with dribbles (25%) and pressure resistance % (15%), among other players who play the same position.
What are some attributes of a winger with a good passing?

Wingers who have a strong passing ability are able to make various types of dangerous passes. They can cross the ball, progress the ball into the final third and complete passes within the final third.
How do we measure if a winger provides for their teammates?

A winger who provides for their teammates ﻿makes a lot of key passes, assists and second assists. They will rank highly in expected goals created and expected assists. Deep completions are also important.
What are the qualities of a goal scoring winger?

The primary quality of a goal scoring winger is that they score goals at high rate per ninety. But it is also important to look at how many chances they get (even if they don't score), which we measure with the expected goals and expected goals on target per ninety metrics.
How would you describe a winger who is not above average in any metrics?
A winger who is not above average in any metrics could be described as not being a standout in any area.
What qualities do we use to evaluate a winger?
We evaluate wingers by their involvement, their passing quality, their ability to provide for teammates, their box threat, their finishing, their dribbling, their run quality and their pressing.
What makes a winger strong technically?

A winger who is good in providing for their teammates and dribbling would be defined as strong technically. A winger who is bad in providing for teammates and dribbling would be defined as poor technically.
What are the metric which measure if a winger has box threat?

The key to a wingers having high box threat is that they get in to the box with the ball and receive the balls in the penalty area. Additionally they should touch the ball alot in the box, score goals and have high expected goal shots.
What metrics tell us that a winger is strong in dribbling?

A good dribbling winger provides attacking threat with their dribbles. They will have a high dribbling success and have high expected threat (xT) from their dribbles. They will also have high expected goals created with dribbles, which measures whether their dribbles lead to good quality shots.
What are the most important metrics for a winger?

How often they contribute and are expected to contribute goals (np goals per ninety, assists per ninety, np expected goals per ninety, expected assists per ninety, chances created per ninety) as well as how good they are at running with the ball (progressive runs per ninety) are generally the most important data-points for a winger.
Why is dribbling not a part of run quality?

Run quality assesses the ability of players to make threatening runs without taking on players. Dribbling past players is a separate quality which is not necessarily correlated with run quality. However, the best players can do both and therefore pose a greater threat.
What can we infer from a winger that is good in terms of  run quality?
Players who rank highly in making runs tend to be faster, as they use their pace to make threatening runs and receive the ball behind the defensive line.
What metrics tell us that a winger is good at pressing?
A winger who presses well has lots high recoveries and makes interceptions. They have a high defence intensity and engage in counterpressing.

What is a winger?

A winger is the football player whose primary role is to receive the ball on the wide channels and create goal threat via dribbling, passing, and shooting.  Wingers have a variety of roles. Inverted wingers are tasked to cut-inside from the wing towards the goal and either shoot or pass. Traditional wingers are expected to dribble down the sideline before passing (or crossing) the ball into the box. In many teams, wingers have the responsibility of being one of the main creative outlets, as well as the fastest and most technically-gifted player.

Dribbling is a weighted sum of a players performance compared to other players in the same position in dribbles success % (20%), dribbles (xT) (40%), expected goals created with dribbles (25%) and pressure resistance % (15%).
What is dribbling?

Dribbling involves the skill of taking on opposing players one-on-one. It's the ability of maneuvering the ball past defenders while maintaining control, often through quick changes in direction, feints, and close ball control.
What do clubs look for when scouting wingers?

A winger who presses well has lots high recoveries and makes interceptions. They have a high defence intensity and engage in counterpressing.

A winger who is good in providing for their teammates and dribbling would be defined as strong technically. A winger who is bad in providing for teammates and dribbling would be defined as poor technically.

A winger with good ball retention is able to keep the ball at a high rate when they attempt dribbles. They rarely lose the ball and are trusted to receive and push the ball into dangerous and tight spaces.

The primary quality of a good finisher is that they score goals at high rate per ninety. But it is also important to look at how often they convert the chances they get and if they have high quality chances on target.
What does it mean for a player to be bad in dribbling?
Players who are bad in dribbling either struggle to dribble past defenders or do not attempt to do so.

We evaluate wingers by their involvement, their passing quality, their ability to provide for teammates, their box threat, their finishing, their dribbling, their run quality and their pressing.

What makes a winger strong technically?

A winger who is good in providing for their teammates and dribbling would be defined as strong technically. A winger who is bad in providing for teammates and dribbling would be defined as poor technically.
What are the most important metrics for a winger?

How often they contribute and are expected to contribute goals (np goals per ninety, assists per ninety, np expected goals per ninety, expected assists per ninety, chances created per ninety) as well as how good they are at running with the ball (progressive runs per ninety) are generally the most important data-points for a winger.
What does it mean for a player to have a high passes (xT)?
A player with a high passes (xT) is able to create a lot of expected threat from passes, and is adept at progressing the ball into more dangerous positions.
How is passing quality calculated?

Passing quality is calculated as the weighted sum of the z-scores of players in passes (xT) (30%), crosses (xT) (20%),  passes into the final third (20 %), passes in the final third (20%) and chance creating passes (10%), among other players who play the same position.
What metrics tell us that a winger is strong in dribbling?

A good dribbling winger provides attacking threat with their dribbles. They will have a high dribbling success and have high expected threat (xT) from their dribbles. They will also have high expected goals created with dribbles, which measures whether their dribbles lead to good quality shots.
What does it mean for a player to have good passing quality?

Players with good passing quality have the ability to consistently deliver different types of passes that pose a significant threat to the opposition's defense. Their passes often lead to goal-scoring opportunities or advantageous positions for their teammates.
What are the important attributes of a winger who has good involvement?
A winger is considered to have good involvement if they are active defensively, have lots of touches on the ball and are involved in play leading up to a shot.
Why is it important to have a winger with a high level of pressing?

Players who rank highly in making runs tend to be faster, as they use their pace to make threatening runs and receive the ball behind the defensive line.
What is a winger?

A winger is the football player whose primary role is to receive the ball on the wide channels and create goal threat via dribbling, passing, and shooting.  Wingers have a variety of roles. Inverted wingers are tasked to cut-inside from the wing towards the goal and either shoot or pass. Traditional wingers are expected to dribble down the sideline before passing (or crossing) the ball into the box. In many teams, wingers have the responsibility of being one of the main creative outlets, as well as the fastest and most technically-gifted player.

What is passing quality?

Passing quality refers to a player's ability to deliver a variety of passes that pose a significant threat to the opposition's defense, leading to goal-scoring opportunities or advantageous positions for the receiving player. It is evaluated by how threatening the passes are, rather than the quantity.
How important is dribbling for a winger?

Dribbling can be an important attribute for a winger, as they are expected to often create threat out of nothing using their pace and technical ability. Wingers can make up for low ranking in dribbling with other skills.

A winger who wins aerial duels, who ranks highly in attacking aerials in particular is considered to have aerial threat. They will tend to head the ball a lot.
How do we measure if a winger provides for their teammates?

A winger who provides for their teammates ﻿makes a lot of key passes, assists and second assists. They will rank highly in expected goals created and expected assists. Deep completions are also important.

A winger with good ball retention is able to keep the ball at a high rate when they attempt dribbles. They rarely lose the ball and are trusted to receive and push the ball into dangerous and tight spaces.
What qualities do we use to evaluate a winger?
We evaluate wingers by their involvement, their passing quality, their ability to provide for teammates, their box threat, their finishing, their dribbling, their run quality and their pressing.
What are the most important attributes for a winger?

There is no undeniable most important attribute for a winger. Some would argue that dribbling is most important. Others would argue that it is goal scoring and assisting. In some systems, perhaps progressing the ball and pressing is most important if they play a more reserved role.
What are some attributes of a winger with a good passing?

Wingers who have a strong passing ability are able to make various types of dangerous passes. They can cross the ball, progress the ball into the final third and complete passes within the final third.
How is passing quality measured?

Passing quality is a weighted sum of a players performance compared to other players in the same position in passes (xT) (30%), crosses (xT) (20%),  passes into the final third (20 %), passes in the final third (20%) and chance passes (10%).
What are the metric which measure if a winger has box threat?

The key to a wingers having high box threat is that they get in to the box with the ball and receive the balls in the penalty area. Additionally they should touch the ball alot in the box, score goals and have high expected goal shots.
What do clubs look for when scouting wingers?

Simply put, good wingers increase their team's chances of scoring a goal. This can be done in a variety of ways, such as dribbling, passing, and shooting. The best wingers in the world can do all three at a high level. Additionally, it is an added benefit if the player is both good at making runs, as well as pressing.

A winger who is good in providing for teammates but not ranked highly in run quality is selfless but does not make himself available in return. We see this happen with wingers make good passes but then hide (in that they don't find a way to receive) or don't dare to make their own runs.

A winger who presses well has lots high recoveries and makes interceptions. They have a high defence intensity and engage in counterpressing.
What makes a winger a strong finisher?

Wingers with excellent finishing skills tend to exhibit a notably high shot conversion percentage. Furthermore, another sign of their prowess in finishing is when they surpass their expected goals by scoring more frequently or consistently placing their shots in optimal positions, indicating a superior ability to convert opportunities compared to their expected goal values.
What are the important metrics for a winger who is good at finishing?

The primary quality of a good finisher is that they score goals at high rate per ninety. But it is also important to look at how often they convert the chances they get and if they have high quality chances on target.
What are the qualities of a goal scoring winger?

The primary quality of a goal scoring winger is that they score goals at high rate per ninety. But it is also important to look at how many chances they get (even if they don't score), which we measure with the expected goals and expected goals on target per ninety metrics.

Players with bad passing quality often choose safer passing options and struggle to deliver threatening passes.

The key to a winger's run quality is making threatening runs with and without the ball and carrying the ball forward. Wingers who are good at runs take the ball into the box themselves and have a high number of penalty area receptions.
How would you describe a winger who  is good in almost all metrics?

What do clubs look for when scouting wingers?

Simply put, good wingers increase their team's chances of scoring a goal. This can be done in a variety of ways, such as dribbling, passing, and shooting. How do we measure if a winger provides for their teammates?

What are the qualities of a goal scoring winger?

The primary quality of a goal scoring winger is that they score goals at high rate per ninety. But it is also important to look at how many chances they get (even if they don't score), which we measure with the expected goals and expected goals on target per ninety metrics.
Why is it important to have a winger with a high level of pressing?

What are the important metrics for a winger who is good at finishing?

What are the important attributes of a winger who has good involvement?
A winger is considered to have good involvement if they are active defensively, have lots of touches on the ball and are involved in play leading up to a shot.

Dribbling can be an important attribute for a winger, as they are expected to often create threat out of nothing using their pace and technical ability. Wingers can make up for low ranking in dribbling with other skills.

Inverted wingers are tasked to cut-inside from the wing towards the goal and either shoot or pass. Traditional wingers are expected to dribble down the sideline before passing (or crossing) the ball into the box. In many teams, wingers have the responsibility of being one of the main creative outlets, as well as the fastest and most technically-gifted player.
What metrics tell us that a winger is good at pressing?

What metrics tell us that a winger is strong in dribbling?

A good dribbling winger provides attacking threat with their dribbles. They will have a high dribbling success and have high expected threat (xT) from their dribbles. They will also have high expected goals created with dribbles, which measures whether their dribbles lead to good quality shots.

Players who rank highly in making runs tend to be faster, as they use their pace to make threatening runs and receive the ball behind the defensive line.
What measurements would convince us that a winger has a high aerial threat?
A winger who wins aerial duels, who ranks highly in attacking aerials in particular is considered to have aerial threat. They will tend to head the ball a lot.

A winger who is good in providing for teammates but not ranked highly in run quality is selfless but does not make himself available in return. We see this happen with wingers make good passes but then hide (in that they don't find a way to receive) or don't dare to make their own runs.

What can we infer from a winger that is good in both making runs and dribbling?
Players who are strong in both making runs and dribbling are likely to be faster and more agile, along with having the technical ability to carry the ball long distances and retain it.
How important is dribbling for a winger?

Dribbling can be an important attribute for a winger, as they are expected to often create threat out of nothing using their pace and technical ability. Wingers can make up for low ranking in dribbling with other skills.
What makes a winger strong technically?

A winger who is good in providing for their teammates and dribbling would be defined as strong technically. A winger who is bad in providing for teammates and dribbling would be defined as poor technically.
What are the metric which measure if a winger has box threat?

The key to a wingers having high box threat is that they get in to the box with the ball and receive the balls in the penalty area. Additionally they should touch the ball alot in the box, score goals and have high expected goal shots.
Why is it important to have a winger with a high level of pressing?

Wingers with high pressing are typically harder-working and are able to help the team's defence by spearheading their pressing attempts. They are very important to modern attacks which rely on pressing and counterpressing to win the ball back.
How would you describe a winger who is not above average in any metrics?

Wingers with excellent finishing skills tend to exhibit a notably high shot conversion percentage. Furthermore, another sign of their prowess in finishing is when they surpass their expected goals by scoring more frequently or consistently placing their shots in optimal positions, indicating a superior ability to convert opportunities compared to their expected goal values.
What do clubs look for when scouting wingers?

Simply put, good wingers increase their team's chances of scoring a goal. This can be done in a variety of ways, such as dribbling, passing, and shooting. The best wingers in the world can do all three at a high level. Additionally, it is an added benefit if the player is both good at making runs, as well as pressing.
What are the important attributes of a winger who has good involvement?

What metrics tell us that a winger is good at pressing?
A winger who presses well has lots high recoveries and makes interceptions. They have a high defence intensity and engage in counterpressing.

What metrics tell us that a winger is strong in dribbling?

What are the important metrics for a winger who is good at finishing?

What are the most important attributes for a winger?

The key to a winger's run quality is making threatening runs with and without the ball and carrying the ball forward. Wingers who are good at runs take the ball into the box themselves and have a high number of penalty area receptions.
What is a winger?

A winger is the football player whose primary role is to receive the ball on the wide channels and create goal threat via dribbling, passing, and shooting.  Wingers have a variety of roles. Inverted wingers are tasked to cut-inside from the wing towards the goal and either shoot or pass. Traditional wingers are expected to dribble down the sideline before passing (or crossing) the ball into the box. In many teams, wingers have the responsibility of being one of the main creative outlets, as well as the fastest and most technically-gifted player.

What does it mean for a winger to be good in ball retention?

A winger with good ball retention is able to keep the ball at a high rate when they attempt dribbles. They rarely lose the ball and are trusted to receive and push the ball into dangerous and tight spaces.

A winger who is good in providing for teammates but not ranked highly in run quality is selfless but does not make himself available in return. We see this happen with wingers make good passes but then hide (in that they don't find a way to receive) or don't dare to make their own runs.
What are some attributes of a winger with a good passing?

Wingers who have a strong passing ability are able to make various types of dangerous passes. They can cross the ball, progress the ball into the final third and complete passes within the final third.
What are the qualities of a goal scoring winger?

The primary quality of a goal scoring winger is that they score goals at high rate per ninety. But it is also important to look at how many chances they get (even if they don't score), which we measure with the expected goals and expected goals on target per ninety metrics.

What are the metric which measure if a winger has box threat?

The key to a wingers having high box threat is that they get in to the box with the ball and receive the balls in the penalty area. Additionally they should touch the ball alot in the box, score goals and have high expected goal shots.
How is box threat measured?

Box threat is a weighted sum of a players performance compared to other players in the same position in touches in box (20%), box entries from carries (10%), goals (25%), expected goals (25%) and penalty area receptions (20%).
What can we infer from a winger that is good in terms of  run quality?

What are some attributes of a winger with a good run quality?

What is a winger?

Inverted wingers are tasked to cut-inside from the wing towards the goal and either shoot or pass. Traditional wingers are expected to dribble down the sideline before passing (or crossing) the ball into the box. In many teams, wingers have the responsibility of being one of the main creative outlets, as well as the fastest and most technically-gifted player.

We evaluate wingers by their involvement, their passing quality, their ability to provide for teammates, their box threat, their finishing, their dribbling, their run quality and their pressing.
How do we measure if a winger provides for their teammates?

What makes a winger strong technically?

A winger who wins aerial duels, who ranks highly in attacking aerials in particular is considered to have aerial threat. They will tend to head the ball a lot.
How is box threat calculated?

Box threat is calculated as the weighted sum of the z-scores of players in touches in box (20%), box entries from carries (10%), non-penalty goals (25%), non-penalty expected goals (25%) and box receptions (20%), among other players who play the same position.

Why are assists not a part of box threat?

Box threat focuses on the goal-scoring threat and involvement of players inside of the penalty are, rather than their creation. Metrics such as assists, expected assists and key passes are represented in the quality providing teammates.

Box threat focuses on the goal-scoring threat and involvement of players inside of the penalty are, rather than their creation. Metrics such as assists, expected assists and key passes are represented in the quality providing teammates.

What does it mean for a player to have a high box threat?

What metrics tell us that a winger is strong in dribbling?

A good dribbling winger provides attacking threat with their dribbles. They will have a high dribbling success and have high expected threat (xT) from their dribbles. They will also have high expected goals created with dribbles, which measures whether their dribbles lead to good quality shots.

A winger who is good in providing for teammates but not ranked highly in run quality is selfless but does not make himself available in return. We see this happen with wingers make good passes but then hide (in that they don't find a way to receive) or don't dare to make their own runs.

A winger is considered to have good involvement if they are active defensively, have lots of touches on the ball and are involved in play leading up to a shot.

A winger who is not above average in any metrics could be described as not being a standout in any area.
What are the important metrics for a winger who is good at finishing?

The primary quality of a good finisher is that they score goals at high rate per ninety. But it is also important to look at how often they convert the chances they get and if they have high quality chances on target.
What metrics tell us that a winger is good at pressing?
A winger who presses well has lots high recoveries and makes interceptions. They have a high defence intensity and engage in counterpressing.

How often they contribute and are expected to contribute goals (np goals per ninety, assists per ninety, np expected goals per ninety, expected assists per ninety, chances created per ninety) as well as how good they are at running with the ball (progressive runs per ninety) are generally the most important data-points for a winger.

What qualities do we use to evaluate a winger?
We evaluate wingers by their involvement, their passing quality, their ability to provide for teammates, their box threat, their finishing, their dribbling, their run quality and their pressing.
What does it mean for a player to be bad in pressing?

Players who struggle with pressing may contribute less defensively and find it challenging to disrupt the opponent's play, which isn't solely linked to their defensive work rate, as it can result from unsuccessful efforts.
What are the qualities of a goal scoring winger?

The primary quality of a goal scoring winger is that they score goals at high rate per ninety. But it is also important to look at how many chances they get (even if they don't score), which we measure with the expected goals and expected goals on target per ninety metrics.

A winger who provides for their teammates ﻿makes a lot of key passes, assists and second assists. They will rank highly in expected goals created and expected assists. Deep completions are also important.
What are the most important metrics for a winger?

How often they contribute and are expected to contribute goals (np goals per ninety, assists per ninety, np expected goals per ninety, expected assists per ninety, chances created per ninety) as well as how good they are at running with the ball (progressive runs per ninety) are generally the most important data-points for a winger.

How is pressing  measured?

Pressing  is a weighted sum of a players performance compared to other players in the same position in defensive intensity (25%), high recoveries (35%), interceptions (10%) and counterpressing recoveries (30%).
Why are high recoveries a part of pressing?

What is a winger?

A winger is the football player whose primary role is to receive the ball on the wide channels and create goal threat via dribbling, passing, and shooting.  Wingers have a variety of roles. Inverted wingers are tasked to cut-inside from the wing towards the goal and either shoot or pass. Traditional wingers are expected to dribble down the sideline before passing (or crossing) the ball into the box. In many teams, wingers have the responsibility of being one of the main creative outlets, as well as the fastest and most technically-gifted player.
What metrics tell us that a winger is good at pressing?
A winger who presses well has lots high recoveries and makes interceptions. They have a high defence intensity and engage in counterpressing.
What are the most important attributes for a winger?

There is no undeniable most important attribute for a winger. Some would argue that dribbling is most important. Others would argue that it is goal scoring and assisting. In some systems, perhaps progressing the ball and pressing is most important if they play a more reserved role.

What is pressing?

Pressing assesses players' proactive defensive efforts to close down, pressure, or engage an opponent with the ball. It takes into account the number of defensive actions players perform, with an emphasis on counterpressing and high recoveries.
What is the relationship between high recoveries and counterpressures?
Counterpressures are often performed after the team loses possession high up the pitch, so a successfull counterpressure usually results in an interception from that player or a teammate.

What measurements would convince us that a winger has a high aerial threat?
A winger who wins aerial duels, who ranks highly in attacking aerials in particular is considered to have aerial threat. They will tend to head the ball a lot.
What does it mean for a player to be good in pressing?
Players who are good in pressing have a high defensive work rate and are skilled in winning possession high up on the pitch, which can generate dangerous offensive transitions.
What are the important attributes of a winger who has good involvement?
A winger is considered to have good involvement if they are active defensively, have lots of touches on the ball and are involved in play leading up to a shot.
What are the metric which measure if a winger has box threat?

What does it mean for a winger to be good in ball retention?

A winger with good ball retention is able to keep the ball at a high rate when they attempt dribbles. They rarely lose the ball and are trusted to receive and push the ball into dangerous and tight spaces.
What makes a winger strong technically?

A winger who is good in providing for their teammates and dribbling would be defined as strong technically. A winger who is bad in providing for teammates and dribbling would be defined as poor technically.
How important is dribbling for a winger?

Dribbling can be an important attribute for a winger, as they are expected to often create threat out of nothing using their pace and technical ability. Wingers can make up for low ranking in dribbling with other skills.
What are some attributes of a winger with a good run quality?

The key to a winger's run quality is making threatening runs with and without the ball and carrying the ball forward. Wingers who are good at runs take the ball into the box themselves and have a high number of penalty area receptions.
Why is it important to have a winger with a high level of pressing?

Wingers with high pressing are typically harder-working and are able to help the team's defence by spearheading their pressing attempts. They are very important to modern attacks which rely on pressing and counterpressing to win the ball back.
What do clubs look for when scouting wingers?

Simply put, good wingers increase their team's chances of scoring a goal. This can be done in a variety of ways, such as dribbling, passing, and shooting. The best wingers in the world can do all three at a high level. Additionally, it is an added benefit if the player is both good at making runs, as well as pressing.

A winger who is not above average in any metrics could be described as not being a standout in any area.
What metrics tell us that a winger is strong in dribbling?

A good dribbling winger provides attacking threat with their dribbles. They will have a high dribbling success and have high expected threat (xT) from their dribbles. They will also have high expected goals created with dribbles, which measures whether their dribbles lead to good quality shots.

A winger who is good in providing for teammates but not ranked highly in run quality is selfless but does not make himself available in return. We see this happen with wingers make good passes but then hide (in that they don't find a way to receive) or don't dare to make their own runs.

Players who rank highly in making runs tend to be faster, as they use their pace to make threatening runs and receive the ball behind the defensive line.

A player who ranks highly in counterpressures and defensive intensity has a high defensive engagement and agresssion, and has a good work rate to attempt win the ball back.

Pressing is calculated as the weighted sum of the z-scores of players in defensive intensity (25%), high recoveries (35%), interceptions (10%) and counterpressing recoveries (30%), among other players who play the same position.

Why are aerials won a part of aerial threat?

While aerial threat primarily assesses a player's offensive danger in the air, it's important to consider their overall aerial strength. Players who consistently win aerial duels demonstrate greater aerial prowess and, consequently, a heightened aerial threat.
What can we infer from a winger that is good in terms of  run quality?
Players who rank highly in making runs tend to be faster, as they use their pace to make threatening runs and receive the ball behind the defensive line.
How would you describe a winger who is not above average in any metrics?
A winger who is not above average in any metrics could be described as not being a standout in any area.
How is aerial threat calculated?

Aerial threat is calculated as the weighted sum of the z-scores of players in aerials won (10%), aerials won % (15%), attacking aerials won (20%), attacking aerials won % (35%) and headed plays (20%), among other players who play the same position.
What are some attributes of a winger with a good passing?

Wingers who have a strong passing ability are able to make various types of dangerous passes. They can cross the ball, progress the ball into the final third and complete passes within the final third.
How important are 'attacking aerials won' for a player's aerial threat?
Attacking aerials won'  are crucial for a player, indicating their ability to win headers in offensive situations, particularly in creating scoring opportunities or directing headers on target.
What do clubs look for when scouting wingers?

Simply put, good wingers increase their team's chances of scoring a goal. This can be done in a variety of ways, such as dribbling, passing, and shooting. The best wingers in the world can do all three at a high level. Additionally, it is an added benefit if the player is both good at making runs, as well as pressing.
Why are headed plays a part of aerial threat?

A player's ability to successfully pass the ball with their head and head the ball towards the goal is indicative of their aerial threat. It shows that they are able to control the ball with their head and to get into goal-scoring positions.
What measurements would convince us that a winger has a high aerial threat?
A winger who wins aerial duels, who ranks highly in attacking aerials in particular is considered to have aerial threat. They will tend to head the ball a lot.
What makes a winger strong technically?

A winger who is good in providing for their teammates and dribbling would be defined as strong technically. A winger who is bad in providing for teammates and dribbling would be defined as poor technically.

How often they contribute and are expected to contribute goals (np goals per ninety, assists per ninety, np expected goals per ninety, expected assists per ninety, chances created per ninety) as well as how good they are at running with the ball (progressive runs per ninety) are generally the most important data-points for a winger.
What does it mean for a player to have a low aerial threat?
Players who rank badly in aerial threat rarely win offensive aerial duels and usually do not pose a goal-scoring danger in the air.
What does it mean for a winger to be good in ball retention?

A winger with good ball retention is able to keep the ball at a high rate when they attempt dribbles. They rarely lose the ball and are trusted to receive and push the ball into dangerous and tight spaces.
What can we infer from a winger that is good in both making runs and dribbling?
Players who are strong in both making runs and dribbling are likely to be faster and more agile, along with having the technical ability to carry the ball long distances and retain it.

Wingers with excellent finishing skills tend to exhibit a notably high shot conversion percentage. A winger who is good in providing for their teammates and dribbling would be defined as strong technically. A winger who is bad in providing for teammates and dribbling would be defined as poor technically.

A winger who is not above average in any metrics could be described as not being a standout in any area.

We evaluate wingers by their involvement, their passing quality, their ability to provide for teammates, their box threat, their finishing, their dribbling, their run quality and their pressing.

A winger is considered to have good involvement if they are active defensively, have lots of touches on the ball and are involved in play leading up to a shot.

Wingers who have a strong passing ability are able to make various types of dangerous passes. They can cross the ball, progress the ball into the final third and complete passes within the final third.

A player's overall 'aerial threat' directly influences their role in set-pieces. Players with high skill in aerial threat are often targeted in offensive set-pieces for headers.

A good dribbling winger provides attacking threat with their dribbles. They will have a high dribbling success and have high expected threat (xT) from their dribbles. They will also have high expected goals created with dribbles, which measures whether their dribbles lead to good quality shots.
